title.zh: 卷三百七十三 列傳第一百三十二 朱弁 鄭望之 張邵 洪皓
title.en: Volume 373 Biographies 132: Zhu Bian, Zheng Wangzhi, Zhang Shao, Hong Hao
title.raw: 卷三百七十三 列傳第一百三十二 朱弁 鄭望之 張邵 洪皓 Volume 373 Biographies 132: Zhu Bian, Zheng Wangzhi, Zhang Shao, Hong Hao

sentences.zh: 朱弁，字少章，徽州婺源人。

translations.literal: Zhu Bian, styled Shaozhang, was a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bian, styled Shaozhang, was from Wuyuan in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟，讀書日數千言。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally quick-witted and read several thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright and could read several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 既冠，入太學，晁說之見其詩，奇之，與歸新鄭，妻以兄女。

translations.literal: After coming of age he entered the Imperial University; Chao Shuozhi saw his poetry, marveled at it, took him home to Xinzheng, and gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After he came of age he entered the Imperial University. Chao Shuozhi saw his poetry, was struck by it, took him back to Xinzheng, and married him to his elder brother's daughter.

sentences.zh: 新鄭介汴、洛間，多故家遺俗，弁遊其中，聞見日廣。

translations.literal: Xinzheng lay between Bian and Luo, where many old families and inherited customs remained; Bian traveled among them, and his knowledge and experience grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzheng lay between Bianjing and Luoyang, where many old families and inherited customs still flourished. As Bian moved among them, what he heard and saw broadened day by day.

sentences.zh: 靖康之亂，家碎於賊，弁南歸。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of the Jingkang era his family was shattered by bandits, and Bian fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingkang turmoil broke out, his family was destroyed by bandits, and Bian fled south.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，議遣使問安兩宮，弁奮身自獻，詔補修武郎，借吉州團練使，為通問副使。

translations.literal: Early in the Jianyan period, when envoys were discussed to inquire after the welfare of the two palaces, Bian stepped forward of his own accord; he was appointed Supplementary Xiowu Lang, lent the title of Regiment Commander of Jizhou, and made Vice Envoy for Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan reign, when the court debated sending envoys to inquire after the two imperial personages in the north, Bian volunteered himself. He was appointed Supplementary Xiowu Lang, lent the title of Regiment Commander of Jizhou, and made vice envoy for communication.

sentences.zh: 至雲中，見粘罕，邀說甚切。

translations.literal: When he reached Yunzhong he saw Nianhan and urged his case with great earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yunzhong he met Nianhan and pressed his arguments with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 粘罕不聽，使就館，守之以兵。

translations.literal: Nianhan would not listen; he had Bian lodged in the guest quarters and guarded with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan would not listen. He had Bian lodged in the guest residence and kept him under armed guard.

sentences.zh: 弁復與書，言用兵講和利害甚悉。

translations.literal: Bian wrote again, setting forth the advantages and disadvantages of warfare and peace in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Bian wrote again, explaining the advantages and disadvantages of war and peace in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，金人忽遣宇文虛中來，言和議可成，當遣一人詣元帥府受書還，虛中欲弁與正使王倫探策決去留，弁曰：「吾來，固自分必死，豈應今日覬幸先歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing the Jurchens suddenly sent Yuwen Xu Zhong, saying peace could be achieved if one man went to the marshal's headquarters to receive the letter and return; Xu Zhong wished Bian and the chief envoy Wang Lun to feel out the situation and decide whether to stay or go. Bian said: "When I came, I fully expected to die; how could I today hope to be the first to return?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing the Jurchens suddenly sent Yuwen Xu Zhong, saying that peace could be achieved if one man went to the marshal's headquarters to receive the letter and return. Xu Zhong wanted Bian and the chief envoy Wang Lun to feel out the situation and decide whether to stay or go. Bian said, "When I came north I had already resigned myself to death. How could I now hope to be the first to return home?"

sentences.zh: 願正使受書歸報天子，成兩國之好，蚤申四海之養於兩宮，則吾雖暴骨外國，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: I wish the chief envoy to receive the letter and return to report to the Son of Heaven, to complete the good relations of the two states and soon extend the nurture of all within the four seas to the two palaces—then though my bones lie exposed in a foreign land, it will still be as the years of my life.
translations.idiomatic: Let the chief envoy take the letter and return to report to the Son of Heaven, so that the two states may be reconciled and the nurture of all under Heaven may soon be restored to the two palaces. Then even if my bones lie exposed in a foreign land, it will still count as living out my years.

sentences.zh: 」倫將歸，弁請曰：「古之使者有節以為信，今無節有印，印亦信也。

translations.literal: " When Wang Lun was about to return, Bian requested: "Ancient envoys had tallies as tokens of trust; today we have no tally but we have a seal, and the seal is also a token of trust.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Lun was about to return, Bian asked, "In antiquity envoys carried tallies as tokens of office. Today we have no tally, but we have a seal—and the seal is a token too.

sentences.zh: 願留印，使弁得抱以死，死不腐矣。

translations.literal: I beg that the seal be left behind, so that Bian may clasp it when he dies; then death will not corrupt me.
translations.idiomatic: Please leave the seal with me, so that I may hold it when I die. Then even in death I shall not be disgraced."

sentences.zh: 」倫解以授弁，弁受而懷之，臥起與俱。

translations.literal: " Wang Lun unfastened it and gave it to Bian; Bian received it and kept it in his bosom, taking it with him whether he lay down or rose.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun unfastened it and gave it to Bian. Bian received it, kept it in his bosom, and never parted from it waking or sleeping.

sentences.zh: 金人迫弁仕劉豫，且訹之曰：「此南歸之漸。

translations.literal: The Jurchens pressed Bian to serve Liu Yu, and moreover tempted him, saying: "This is the first step toward returning south."
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pressed Bian to serve Liu Yu and tempted him, saying, "This is the first step on the road home to the south."

sentences.zh: 」弁曰：「豫乃國賊，吾嘗恨不食其肉，又忍北面臣之，吾有死耳。

translations.literal: " Bian said: "Yu is a traitor to the state; I have long regretted that I could not eat his flesh—how could I bear to face north and serve him as subject? I have only death."
translations.idiomatic: Bian replied, "Yu is a traitor to our state. I have long regretted that I could not eat his flesh—how could I bear to face north and serve him as my lord? I have only death."

sentences.zh: 」金人怒，絕其餼遺以困之。

translations.literal: " The Jurchens were enraged and cut off his provisions to wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were enraged and cut off his rations to break him.

sentences.zh: 弁固拒驛門，忍飢待盡，誓不為屈。

translations.literal: Bian firmly barred the post-house gate, endured hunger awaiting death, and swore never to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Bian barred the gate of the post-house, endured hunger to the point of death, and swore never to submit.

sentences.zh: 金人亦感動，緻禮如初。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were also moved and restored his provisions as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were moved as well and restored his provisions as before.

sentences.zh: 久之，复欲易其官，弁曰：「自古兵交，使在其間，言可從從之，不可從則囚之、殺之，何必易其官？

translations.literal: After a long time they again wished to change his office. Bian said: "Since antiquity, when states are at war, envoys stand between them: if their words may be followed, they are followed; if not, they are imprisoned or killed—why must their office be changed?
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval they again tried to change his official title. Bian said, "Since antiquity, when states are at war envoys stand between them: if their words are heeded, they are heeded; if not, they are imprisoned or killed. Why must their office be changed?

sentences.zh: 吾官受之本朝，有死而已，誓不易以辱吾君也。

translations.literal: My office was received from our own court; I have only death, and I swear I will not change it to disgrace my sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: My office was granted by our own court. I have only death, and I swear I will not change it to bring shame on my sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」且移書耶律紹文等曰：「上國之威命朝以至，則使人夕以死，夕以至則朝以死。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Yelü Shaowen and others, saying: "When the august command of the superior state arrives in the morning, the envoy dies by evening; when it arrives in the evening, he dies by morning."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Yelü Shaowen and others: "When the august command of your state arrives in the morning, the envoy dies by evening; when it arrives in the evening, he dies by morning."

sentences.zh: 」又以書訣後使洪皓曰：「殺行人非細事，吾曹遭之，命也，要當舍生以全義爾。

translations.literal: He also wrote in farewell to the later envoy Hong Hao: "To kill an envoy is no small matter; that we have met with this is fate, but we must give up our lives to preserve righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a farewell letter to the envoy who came after him, Hong Hao: "To kill an envoy is no trifling matter. That we have met this fate is destiny—but we must give up our lives to preserve righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」乃具酒食，召被掠士夫飲，半酣，語之曰：「吾已得近郊某寺地，一旦畢命報國，諸公幸瘞我其處，題其上曰『有宋通問副使朱公之墓』，於我幸矣。

translations.literal: He then prepared wine and food, summoned captured scholar-officials to drink, and when they were half drunk said to them: "I have already secured ground at a certain monastery in the near suburbs; when I once give up my life to repay the state, I hope you gentlemen will bury me there and inscribe above it 'Tomb of Vice Envoy for Communication of the Song, Lord Zhu'—that would be my good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: He then set out wine and food and summoned captured scholar-officials to drink with him. When they were half drunk he told them, "I have already secured a plot at a monastery in the near suburbs. When I give up my life for the state, I hope you will bury me there and inscribe above it, 'Tomb of Vice Envoy for Communication of the Song, Lord Zhu.' That would be my good fortune."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆泣下，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: " All wept and could not look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: All wept and could not bear to look up at him.

sentences.zh: 弁談笑自若，曰：​​「此臣子之常，諸君何悲也？

translations.literal: Bian talked and laughed as usual and said: "This is what subjects do—why do you gentlemen grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian talked and laughed as usual and said, "This is what subjects are supposed to do—why do you grieve?"

sentences.zh: 」金人知其終不可屈，遂不復強。

translations.literal: " The Jurchens knew he could never be bent and therefore pressed him no further.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens saw that he would never yield and pressed him no further.

sentences.zh: 王倫還朝，言弁守節不屈，帝為官其子林，賜其家銀帛。

translations.literal: When Wang Lun returned to court he reported that Bian had preserved his integrity and would not yield; the Emperor gave office to his son Lin and bestowed silver and silks on his family.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun returned to court he reported that Bian had held fast to his integrity and refused to yield. The emperor gave office to his son Lin and bestowed silver and silks on his family.

sentences.zh: 會粘罕等相繼死滅，弁密疏其事及金國虛實，曰：「此不可失之時也。

translations.literal: When Nianhan and others died in succession, Bian sent a secret memorial on these events and on the true state of the Jin state, saying: "This is a moment that must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: When Nianhan and others died one after another, Bian sent a secret memorial reporting these events and the true condition of the Jin state, saying, "This is a moment that must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 」遣李發等間行歸報。

translations.literal: " He sent Li Fa and others by secret route to return and report.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Fa and others by secret routes to return and report.

sentences.zh: 其後，倫復歸，又以弁奉送徽宗大行之文為獻，其辭有曰：「嘆馬角之未生，魂消雪窖；

translations.literal: Later Wang Lun returned again and also presented, on Bian's behalf, the text composed for the great journey of Emperor Huizong; its wording included: "I sigh that horse-horns have not yet grown—my soul dissolves in the snow cellar;"
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Lun returned again and presented, on Bian's behalf, the memorial composed for the funeral procession of Emperor Huizong. Its wording included: "I sigh that horse-horns have not yet sprouted—my soul wastes away in the snow cellar;"

sentences.zh: 攀龍髯而莫逮，淚灑冰天。

translations.literal: "grasping the dragon's whiskers yet unable to reach them, tears fall upon the icy sky."
translations.idiomatic: "I grasp the dragon's whiskers yet cannot reach them—my tears fall upon the icy sky."

sentences.zh: 」帝讀之感泣，官其親屬五人，賜吳興田五頃。

translations.literal: " The Emperor read it and wept with emotion; he gave office to five of his kinsmen and granted five qing of fields in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and wept. He gave office to five of Bian's kinsmen and granted five qing of fields in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 帝謂丞相張浚曰：「歸日，當以禁林處之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the Chief Councillor Zhang Jun: "When he returns, he should be placed in the Hanlin Academy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Chief Councillor Zhang Jun, "When he returns, he should be placed in the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 」八年，金使烏陵思謀、石慶充至，稱弁忠節，詔附黃金三十兩以賜。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year, Jin envoys Wulingsimou and Shi Qingchong arrived, praised Bian's loyalty and integrity, and an edict attached thirty taels of gold as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jin envoys Wulingsimou and Shi Qingchong arrived, praised Bian's loyalty and integrity, and an edict ordered thirty taels of gold sent as a gift.

sentences.zh: 十三年，和議成，弁得歸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the peace agreement was concluded and Bian was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the peace agreement was concluded and Bian was able to return home.

sentences.zh: 入見便殿，弁謝且曰：「人之所難得者時，而時之運無已；

translations.literal: He entered audience in the side hall, thanked the Emperor, and said: "What men find hard to obtain is opportunity, yet the movement of opportunity never ceases;
translations.idiomatic: He was received in the side hall, thanked the emperor, and said, "What is hardest for men to obtain is opportunity, yet the movement of opportunity never ceases;

sentences.zh: 事之不可失者幾，而幾之藏無形。

translations.literal: what affairs must not be missed is the subtle moment, yet the concealment of the subtle moment has no form.
translations.idiomatic: what must not be missed in affairs is the subtle turning point, yet the subtle turning point hides without form.

sentences.zh: 惟無已也，故來遲而難遇；

translations.literal: Because it never ceases, it comes late and is hard to meet;
translations.idiomatic: Because it never ceases, it arrives late and is hard to seize;

sentences.zh: 惟無形也，故動微而難見。

translations.literal: because it has no form, its movement is slight and hard to perceive.
translations.idiomatic: because it has no form, its movement is slight and hard to perceive.

sentences.zh: 陛下與金人講和，上返梓宮，次迎太母，又其次則憐赤子之無辜，此皆知時知幾之明驗。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has made peace with the Jurchens, first to return the imperial coffin, next to welcome the Grand Empress Dowager, and after that to pity the innocent common people—this is clear proof of knowing the time and the subtle moment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has made peace with the Jurchens—first to bring back the imperial coffin, next to welcome the Grand Empress Dowager, and after that to pity the innocent people. This is clear proof that you know the time and seize the subtle moment.

sentences.zh: 然時運而往，或難固執；

translations.literal: Yet as opportunity moves onward, it may be hard to hold fast;
translations.idiomatic: Yet as opportunity moves on, it may be hard to hold fast;

sentences.zh: 幾動有變，宜鑑未兆。

translations.literal: when the subtle moment stirs there is change, and one should take warning from what has not yet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: when the subtle moment stirs, change follows, and you should take warning from what has not yet appeared.

sentences.zh: 盟可守，而詭詐之心宜嘿以待之；

translations.literal: The alliance may be kept, but treacherous hearts should be met in silence and awaited;
translations.idiomatic: The alliance may be kept, but treacherous intent should be met in silence and watched for;

sentences.zh: 兵可息，而銷弭之術宜詳以講之。

translations.literal: arms may be stilled, but the methods of eliminating and pacifying them should be discussed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: arms may be stilled, but the methods of eliminating and pacifying conflict should be discussed in detail.

sentences.zh: 金人以黷武為至德，以苟安為太平，虐民而不恤民，廣地而不廣德，此皆天助中興之勢。

translations.literal: The Jurchens take addicted warfare as supreme virtue and complacent ease as great peace; they mistreat the people without caring for them and extend territory without extending virtue—all this is Heaven assisting the momentum of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens take addicted warfare as supreme virtue and complacent ease as great peace. They mistreat the people without caring for them and extend territory without extending virtue—all of this is Heaven assisting the momentum of restoration.

sentences.zh: 若時與幾，陛下既知於始，願圖厥終。

translations.literal: If in opportunity and the subtle moment Your Majesty has known them at the beginning, I pray you plan their end."
translations.idiomatic: If in opportunity and the subtle moment Your Majesty has grasped them at the beginning, I pray you plan for their end."

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，賜金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted his words and bestowed gold and silks in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel and bestowed gold and silks in great abundance.

sentences.zh: 弁又以金國所得六朝御容及宣和御書畫為獻。

translations.literal: Bian also presented the imperial portraits of the Six Dynasties and the calligraphy and paintings of the Xuanhe reign obtained in the Jin state.
translations.idiomatic: Bian also presented the imperial portraits of the Six Dynasties and the Xuanhe-era calligraphy and paintings that had been taken by the Jin.

sentences.zh: 秦檜惡其言敵情，奏以初補官易宣教郎、直秘閣。

translations.literal: Qin Hui hated his reports on the enemy situation and memorialized that his initial supplementary appointment be exchanged for Xuanjiao Lang and Direct Secretariat Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui resented his reports on enemy conditions and memorialized that his initial supplementary appointment be exchanged for Xuanjiao Lang and Direct Secretariat Aide.

sentences.zh: 有司校其考十七年，應遷數官。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reviewed his service evaluation of seventeen years and found he should be promoted several ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reviewed his seventeen years of service evaluation and found he should be promoted several ranks.

sentences.zh: 檜沮之，僅轉奉議郎。

translations.literal: Qin Hui obstructed this; he was promoted only to Fengyi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui blocked it, and Bian was promoted only to Fengyi Lang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 弁為文慕陸宣公，援據精博，曲盡事理。

translations.literal: In his writing Bian admired Lu Xuangong; his citations were precise and extensive, and he thoroughly expounded the principles of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his writing Bian took Lu Xuangong as his model. His citations were precise and extensive, and he thoroughly expounded the principles of affairs.

sentences.zh: 詩學李義山，詞氣雍容，不蹈其險怪奇澀之弊。

translations.literal: In poetry he studied Li Yishan; his diction was dignified and easy, and he did not fall into the faults of obscurity, strangeness, and difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he studied Li Shangyin. His diction was dignified and measured, and he avoided the pitfalls of obscurity, strangeness, and difficulty.

sentences.zh: 金國名王貴人多遣子弟就學，弁因文字往來說以和好之利。

translations.literal: Many princes and nobles of the Jin state sent their sons and younger brothers to study; through written exchanges Bian explained to them the benefits of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Many princes and nobles of the Jin sent their sons and younger brothers to study with him. Through written exchanges Bian explained to them the benefits of peace.

sentences.zh: 及歸，述北方所見聞忠臣義士朱昭、史抗、張忠輔、高景平、孫益、孫谷、傅偉文、李舟、五臺僧寶真、婦人丁氏、晏氏、小校閻進、朱勣等死節事狀，請加褒錄以勸來者。

translations.literal: When he returned he recounted what he had seen and heard in the north of loyal ministers and righteous men—Zhu Zhao, Shi Kang, Zhang Zhongfu, Gao Jingping, Sun Yi, Sun Gu, Fu Weiwen, Li Zhou, the Wutai monk Baozhen, the women Ding and Yan, the petty officer Yan Jin, Zhu Ji, and others who died preserving their integrity—and requested enhanced commendation to encourage those who would come after.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he recounted what he had seen and heard in the north concerning loyal ministers and righteous men who died preserving their integrity—Zhu Zhao, Shi Kang, Zhang Zhongfu, Gao Jingping, Sun Yi, Sun Gu, Fu Weiwen, Li Zhou, the Wutai monk Baozhen, the women surnamed Ding and Yan, the petty officer Yan Jin, Zhu Ji, and others—and asked that they be commended posthumously to encourage those who would come after.

sentences.zh: 有《聘遊集》四十二卷、《書解》十卷、《曲洧舊聞》三卷、《續骫骳說》一卷，《雜書》一卷、《風月堂詩話》三卷、《新鄭舊詩》一卷、《南歸詩文》一卷。

translations.literal: He had the Pinyouji in forty-two juan, Shujie in ten juan, Quwo Jiujian in three juan, Xu Weibei Shuo in one juan, Zashu in one juan, Fengyuetang Shihua in three juan, Xinzheng Jiushi in one juan, and Nangui Shiwen in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Pinyouji in forty-two juan, Shujie in ten juan, Quwo Jiujian in three juan, Xu Weibei Shuo in one juan, Zashu in one juan, Fengyuetang Shihua in three juan, Xinzheng Jiushi in one juan, and Nangui Shiwen in one juan.

sentences.zh: 鄭望之

translations.literal: Zheng Wangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wangzhi

sentences.zh: 鄭望之，字顧道，彭城人，顯謨閣直學士僅之子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Wangzhi, styled Gudao, was a native of Pengcheng and the son of Xianmo Pavilion Direct Academician Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wangzhi, styled Gudao, was from Pengcheng and the son of Xianmo Pavilion Direct Academician Jin.

sentences.zh: 望之少有文名，山東皆推重。

translations.literal: Wangzhi early gained a literary reputation, and all east of the mountains esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi gained a literary reputation early, and all east of the mountains held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧五年進士第，自陳留簿累遷樞密院編修官，歷開封府儀、工、戶曹，以治辦稱。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning, rose from Recorder of Chenliu through Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and served in the Ritual, Works, and Revenue sections of the Kaifeng prefecture, being known for effective administration.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning, rose from Recorder of Chenliu to Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and served in the Ritual, Works, and Revenue sections of the Kaifeng prefecture, where he was known for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 臨事勁正，不受請託。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was firm and upright and accepted no private requests.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was firm and upright and accepted no private requests.

sentences.zh: 宦寺有強佔民田者，奏歸之。

translations.literal: When eunuchs forcibly seized commoners' fields he memorialized for their return.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs forcibly seized commoners' fields, he memorialized for their return to the owners.

sentences.zh: 蔡京子欲奪人妾，使人諭意，望之拒不受。

translations.literal: A son of Cai Jing wished to seize another man's concubine and sent someone to convey his intent; Wangzhi refused and would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When a son of Cai Jing wished to seize another man's concubine and sent someone to convey his intent, Wangzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 除駕部員外郎兼金部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Transport Office, concurrently in the Gold Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Transport Office, concurrently serving in the Gold Section.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，金人攻汴京，假尚書工部侍郎，俾為軍前計議使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens attacked Bianjing, he was lent the title of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and made Commissioner for Deliberation before the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens attacked Bianjing, he was lent the title of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and made commissioner for deliberation before the enemy army.

sentences.zh: 既還，金人遣吳孝民與望之同入見。

translations.literal: After he returned, the Jurchens sent Wu Xiaomin to enter audience together with Wangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, the Jurchens sent Wu Xiaomin to enter audience together with Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 望之言金人意在金幣，且要大臣同議，乃命同知樞密院事李棁與望之再使，斡離不以朝廷受歸朝官及賜平州張覺手詔為辭，遣蕭三寶奴偕棁等還，以書求割三鎮，欲得宰相交地，親王送大軍過河。

translations.literal: Wangzhi said the Jurchens' intent lay in gold and coin and that they also wanted high ministers to join in deliberation; the court therefore ordered Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Zhen and Wangzhi to go again as envoys. Woliyan took as his pretext the court's acceptance of officials who had returned to the dynasty and its bestowal of an autograph edict on Zhang Jue of Pingzhou; he sent Xiao Sanbaonu back with Zhen and the others, demanding in a letter the cession of three circuits, wishing to have the chief councillor hand over territory and a prince escort the great army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi reported that the Jurchens wanted gold and coin and also demanded that high ministers join in negotiations. The court therefore ordered Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Zhen and Wangzhi to go again as envoys. Woliyan cited as his pretext the court's acceptance of officials who had returned to the dynasty and its bestowal of an autograph edict on Zhang Jue of Pingzhou. He sent Xiao Sanbaonu back with Zhen and the others, demanding in a letter the cession of three circuits, the chief councillor's handover of territory, and a prince to escort the main army across the river.

sentences.zh: 時高宗在康邸慷慨請行，遂與張邦昌乘筏渡濠，自午至夜分，始達金砦。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozong, then at the Kang residence, volunteered himself with fervor; he and Zhang Bangchang crossed the moat on rafts and from noon until midnight before reaching the Jin camp.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Gaozong, then at the Kang residence, volunteered himself with fervor. He and Zhang Bangchang crossed the moat on rafts and traveled from noon until midnight before reaching the Jin camp.

sentences.zh: 又除望之戶部侍郎，同棁再至金營，仍以珠玉遺金人。

translations.literal: Wangzhi was again appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and went with Zhen once more to the Jin camp, again presenting pearls and jade to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi was again appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and went with Zhen once more to the Jin camp, again presenting pearls and jade to the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 金人拘留望之逾旬。

translations.literal: The Jurchens detained Wangzhi for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens detained Wangzhi for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 會姚平仲夜劫砦不克，斡離不以用兵詰責諸使者，邦昌恐懼涕泣，王不為​​動。

translations.literal: When Yao Pingzhong raided the camp by night but failed, Woliyan rebuked the envoys for the use of troops; Bangchang wept in fear, but the Prince was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Pingzhong raided the camp by night but failed, Woliyan rebuked the envoys for the use of troops. Bangchang wept in fear, but the prince was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 金人遂不欲留王，更請肅王，乃以兵送望之詣國王砦詰問。

translations.literal: The Jurchens then did not wish to detain the Prince and instead asked for Prince Su; they sent troops to escort Wangzhi to the Prince of Guo's camp for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens then did not wish to detain the prince and instead asked for Prince Su. They sent troops to escort Wangzhi to the Prince of Guo's camp for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 會再遣宇文虛中持割地詔至，望之得還，因盛言敵勢強大，我兵削弱，不可不和。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Xu Zhong was again sent bearing the edict ceding territory, Wangzhi was able to return and thereupon spoke at length of the enemy's strength and our army's weakness, saying peace was unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Xu Zhong was again sent bearing the edict ceding territory, Wangzhi was able to return and spoke at length of the enemy's strength and our army's weakness, arguing that peace was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 既而金兵退，朝廷以議和非策，罷望之提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: Soon after the Jin army withdrew, the court regarded negotiation as the wrong policy and dismissed Wangzhi to Superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the Jin army withdrew, the court regarded negotiation as the wrong policy and dismissed Wangzhi to superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，李綱以望之張皇敵勢，沮損國威，以致禍敗，責海州團練副使，連州居住。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan, Li Gang held that Wangzhi had exaggerated the enemy's power, damaged national prestige, and thereby brought on disaster; he was demoted to Vice Regiment Commander of Haizhou and ordered to reside in Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan, Li Gang held that Wangzhi had exaggerated enemy strength, damaged national prestige, and thereby brought on disaster. He was demoted to Vice Regiment Commander of Haizhou and ordered to reside in Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 綱罷，詔望之為戶部侍郎，尋轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gang was dismissed, an edict appointed Wangzhi Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon after he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, an edict appointed Wangzhi Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon after he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 論王雲之冤，帝為感動，復云元官，與七子恩澤。

translations.literal: He argued the injustice done to Wang Yun; the Emperor was moved and restored Yun's former office and granted favors to his seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the injustice done to Wang Yun. The emperor was moved and restored Yun's former office and granted favors to his seven sons.

sentences.zh: 尋兼主管御營司參贊軍事。

translations.literal: Soon after he was concurrently Supervisor of the Imperial Camp Office, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was concurrently made supervisor of the Imperial Camp Office, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 論航海不便，忤旨，以集英殿修撰再領亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: He argued that travel by sea was impracticable, ran counter to the imperial will, and was made Compiler at the Jiying Hall while again heading the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that travel by sea was impracticable, ran counter to the imperial will, and was made Compiler at the Jiying Hall while again heading the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 起知宣州，逾年，以言章罷。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou; after more than a year he was dismissed on a memorial of impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Xuanzhou. After more than a year he was dismissed on a memorial of impeachment.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，會赦，复徽猷閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, when an amnesty was proclaimed, he was again made Huixiu Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing, when an amnesty was proclaimed, he was again made Huixiu Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary and retired.

sentences.zh: 七年，落致仕，召赴行在。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his retirement was revoked and he was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his retirement was revoked and he was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 望之以衰老辭，帝謂大臣曰：「望之，朕故人也。

translations.literal: Wangzhi declined on account of old age; the Emperor said to his high ministers: "Wangzhi is an old friend of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi declined on account of old age. The emperor said to his high ministers, "Wangzhi is an old friend of mine."

sentences.zh: 」於是升徽猷閣直學士，复致仕。

translations.literal: " He was then promoted to Huixiu Pavilion Direct Academician and again retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Huixiu Pavilion Direct Academician and again retired.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he died, aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈中大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年，金人南侵，詔求可至軍前者，邵慨然請行，轉五官，直龍圖閣，假禮部尚書，充通問使，武官楊憲副之，即日就道。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the Jurchens invaded south, an edict sought one who could go before the enemy army; Shao volunteered himself with fervor, was promoted five ranks, made Direct Longtu Pavilion, lent the title of Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and made Envoy for Communication, with the military officer Yang Xian as his deputy; he set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Jurchens invaded south, an edict sought someone who could go before the enemy army. Shao volunteered with fervor, was promoted five ranks, made Direct Longtu Pavilion, lent the title of Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and made envoy for communication, with the military officer Yang Xian as his deputy. He set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 至濰州，接伴使置酒張樂，邵曰：「二帝北遷，邵為臣子，所不忍聽，請止樂。

translations.literal: When he reached Weizhou the receiving envoy set out wine and had music played; Shao said: "The two emperors were taken north—Shao, as their subject, cannot bear to hear this; I beg that the music be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Weizhou the receiving envoy set out wine and had music played. Shao said, "The two emperors were taken north. As their subject I cannot bear to hear this—please stop the music."

sentences.zh: 」至於三四，聞者泣下。

translations.literal: " He repeated this three or four times, and those who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated this three or four times, and those who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 翌日，見左監軍撻攬，命邵拜，邵曰：「監軍與邵為南北朝從臣，無相拜禮。

translations.literal: The next day he saw the Left Overseer Tadan and was ordered to bow; Shao said: "The Overseer and Shao are subjects of the two courts of north and south—there is no mutual bowing ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he saw the Left Overseer Tadan and was ordered to bow. Shao said, "The Overseer and I are subjects of the two courts of north and south—there is no ceremony of mutual bowing."

sentences.zh: 」且以書抵之曰：「兵不在強弱，在曲直。

translations.literal: He also sent him a letter, saying: "In warfare strength and weakness do not matter—what matters is right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent him a letter saying, "In warfare strength and weakness do not matter—what matters is right and wrong."

sentences.zh: 宣和以來，我非無兵也，帥臣初開邊隙，謀臣复啟兵端，是以大國能勝之。

translations.literal: Since the Xuanhe era we have not lacked troops; commanders first opened border conflicts and strategists again provoked warfare, and therefore the great state was able to defeat us.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xuanhe era we have not lacked troops. Our commanders first opened border conflicts and our strategists again provoked warfare—therefore your great state was able to defeat us.

sentences.zh: 厥後偽楚僭立，群盜蜂起，曾幾何時，電掃無餘，是天意人心未厭宋德也。

translations.literal: Afterward the false Chu usurped the throne and bandits rose like bees; in how short a time they were swept away like lightning, leaving nothing—this is Heaven's intent and men's hearts not yet weary of Song virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the false Chu usurped the throne and bandits rose everywhere. In how short a time they were swept away like lightning, leaving nothing—this shows that Heaven's intent and men's hearts have not yet turned against Song virtue.

sentences.zh: 今大國复裂地以封劉豫，窮兵不已，曲有在矣。

translations.literal: Now the great state again carves territory to enfeoff Liu Yu and presses warfare without end—the wrong lies on your side."
translations.idiomatic: Now your great state again carves territory to enfeoff Liu Yu and presses warfare without end—the wrong lies on your side."

sentences.zh: 」撻攬怒，取國書去，執邵送密州，囚於祚山砦。

translations.literal: " Tadan was enraged, took the state letter and left, seized Shao and sent him to Mizhou, and imprisoned him at the Zuoshan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Tadan was enraged, took the state letter and left, seized Shao and sent him to Mizhou, and imprisoned him at the Zuoshan stockade.

sentences.zh: 明年，又送邵於劉豫，使用之。

translations.literal: The next year Shao was again sent to Liu Yu, who employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shao was again sent to Liu Yu, who employed him.

sentences.zh: 邵見劉豫，長揖而已，又呼為「殿院」，責以君臣大義，詞氣俱厲，豫怒，械置於獄，楊憲遂降。

translations.literal: When Shao saw Liu Yu he merely made a long bow, and again addressed him as "Hall Commissioner," rebuking him with the great principle of ruler and subject; his words and tone were both severe. Yu was enraged and had him shackled and placed in prison; Yang Xian then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao saw Liu Yu he merely made a long bow and addressed him as "Hall Commissioner," rebuking him with the great principle of ruler and subject. His words and tone were both severe. Yu was enraged and had him shackled and placed in prison. Yang Xian then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 豫知邵不屈，久之，复送於金，拘之燕山僧寺，從者皆莫知所之。

translations.literal: Yu knew Shao would not yield; after a long time he was again sent to the Jin and detained in a Buddhist monastery at Yanshan; his attendants all vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Yu knew Shao would not yield. After a long interval he was again sent to the Jin and detained in a Buddhist monastery at Yanshan. His attendants all vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 後又作書，為金言「劉豫挾大國之勢，日夜南侵，不勝則首鼠兩端，勝則如養鷹，飽則颺去，終非大國之利」，守者密以告，金取其書去，益北徙之會寧府，距燕三千里。

translations.literal: Later he wrote again, telling the Jin: "Liu Yu relies on the great state's power and invades south day and night. If he fails he will hedge between two sides; if he succeeds he is like a hawk you feed—when full it flies away. In the end this is not to the great state's advantage." The guards secretly reported this; the Jin took his letter and moved him farther north to the Huining prefecture, three thousand li from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he wrote again, telling the Jin: "Liu Yu relies on your great state's power and invades south day and night. If he fails he will hedge between two sides; if he succeeds he is like a hawk you feed—when full it flies away. In the end this does not serve your great state's interests." The guards secretly reported this. The Jin took his letter and moved him farther north to Huining prefecture, three thousand li from Yan.

sentences.zh: 金嘗大赦，許宋使者自便還鄉，人人多佔籍淮北，冀幸稍南。

translations.literal: The Jin once proclaimed a great amnesty and allowed Song envoys to return home at will; most registered their households north of the Huai, hoping to move slightly south.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin once proclaimed a great amnesty and allowed Song envoys to return home at will. Most registered their households north of the Huai, hoping to move slightly south.

sentences.zh: 惟邵與洪皓、朱弁言家在江南。

translations.literal: Only Shao, together with Hong Hao and Zhu Bian, said their families were in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shao, together with Hong Hao and Zhu Bian, said their families were in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，和議成，及皓、弁南歸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the peace agreement was concluded, and Hao and Bian returned south.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the peace agreement was concluded, and Hao and Bian returned south.

sentences.zh: 八月，入見，奏前後使者如陳過庭、司馬樸、滕茂實、崔縱、魏行可皆歿異域未褒贈者，乞早頒卹典。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he entered audience and memorialized that former envoys such as Chen Guoting, Sima Pu, Teng Maoshi, Cui Zong, and Wei Xingke had all died in foreign lands without posthumous honors, and begged that condolence rites be granted soon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he entered audience and memorialized that former envoys such as Chen Guoting, Sima Pu, Teng Maoshi, Cui Zong, and Wei Xingke had all died in foreign lands without posthumous honors, and begged that condolence rites be granted soon.

sentences.zh: 邵並攜崔縱柩歸其家。

translations.literal: Shao also brought Cui Zong's coffin back to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also brought Cui Zong's coffin back to his family.

sentences.zh: 升秘閣修撰，主管佑神觀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler of the Secretariat and made Superintendent of the Youzhen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Secretariat and made superintendent of the Youzhen Observatory.

sentences.zh: 左司諫詹大方論其奉使無成，改台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official of the Left Bureau Zhan Dafang argued that his mission had achieved nothing; he was reassigned to the Chongdao Observatory in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official of the Left Bureau Zhan Dafang argued that his mission had achieved nothing; he was reassigned to the Chongdao Observatory in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 移書時相，勸其迎請欽宗與諸王后妃。

translations.literal: He wrote to the chief councillors urging them to welcome back Emperor Qinzong and the princes, queens, and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the chief councillors urging them to welcome back Emperor Qinzong and the princes, queens, and consorts.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以敷文閣待制提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was made Fuwen Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary and Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made Fuwen Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知池州，再奉祠卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Chizhou, again received a sacrificial appointment, and died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Chizhou, again received a sacrificial appointment, and died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 累贈少師。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted several times to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted several times to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 邵負氣，遇事慷慨，常以功名自許，出使囚徙，屢瀕於死。

translations.literal: Shao was high-spirited; in affairs he was fervent and often pledged himself to achieve fame and merit. As an envoy he was imprisoned and exiled and several times came near death.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was high-spirited. In affairs he was fervent and often pledged himself to achieve fame and merit. As an envoy he was imprisoned and exiled and several times came near death.

sentences.zh: 其在會寧，金人多從之學。

translations.literal: At Huining many Jurchens came to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: At Huining many Jurchens came to study with him.

sentences.zh: 喜誦佛書，雖異域不廢。

translations.literal: He delighted in reciting Buddhist texts and did not abandon this even in a foreign land.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in reciting Buddhist texts and did not abandon this even in a foreign land.

sentences.zh: 初，使金時，遇秦檜於濰州。

translations.literal: When he first went as envoy to the Jin he met Qin Hui at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he first went as envoy to the Jin he met Qin Hui at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 及歸，上書言檜忠節，議者以是少之。

translations.literal: When he returned he memorialized that Hui was loyal and steadfast in integrity; critics therefore thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he memorialized that Hui was loyal and steadfast in integrity; critics therefore thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 後弟祁下大理獄，將株連邵，會檜死得免。

translations.literal: Later his younger brother Qi was imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review and Shao was to be implicated; he was spared when Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Later his younger brother Qi was imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review and Shao was to be implicated; he was spared when Hui died.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子孝覽、孝曾、孝忠。

translations.literal: His sons were Xiaolan, Xiaozeng, and Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiaolan, Xiaozeng, and Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 孝曾後亦以出使歿於金，金人知為邵子，尚憐之。

translations.literal: Xiaozeng later also died in the Jin on an envoy mission; the Jurchens knew he was Shao's son and still pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozeng later also died in the Jin on an envoy mission; the Jurchens knew he was Shao's son and still pitied him.

sentences.zh: 洪皓，字光弼，番昜人。

translations.literal: Hong Hao, styled Guangbi, was a native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hao, styled Guangbi, was from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 少有奇節，慷慨有經略四方志。

translations.literal: In youth he had an unusual integrity, was fervent, and harbored the ambition to govern all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had an unusual integrity, was fervent, and harbored the ambition to govern all four directions.

sentences.zh: 登政和五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 王黼、朱勔皆欲婚之，力辭。

translations.literal: Wang Fu and Zhu Mian both wished to marry him to their families; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu and Zhu Mian both wished to marry him to their families; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，為秀州司錄。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era he served as Recorder of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe era he served as Recorder of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大水，民多失業，皓白郡守以拯荒自任，發廩損直以糶。

translations.literal: When great floods came many people lost their livelihoods; Hao told the prefect he would take famine relief upon himself, opened the granaries, and sold grain at reduced prices.
translations.idiomatic: When great floods came many people lost their livelihoods. Hao told the prefect he would take famine relief upon himself, opened the granaries, and sold grain at reduced prices.

sentences.zh: 民坌集，皓恐其紛競，乃別以青白幟，涅其手以識之，令嚴而惠遍。

translations.literal: The people crowded in; Hao feared disorder and therefore used blue and white banners separately, marked their hands with ink to identify them, and made the regulations strict while benefits reached all.
translations.idiomatic: The people crowded in. Hao feared disorder and therefore used blue and white banners separately, marked their hands with ink to identify them, and made the regulations strict while benefits reached all.

sentences.zh: 浙東綱米過城下，皓白守邀留之，守不可，皓曰：「願以一身易十萬人命。

translations.literal: When the Zhedong transport grain passed below the city wall, Hao told the prefect to detain it; the prefect would not agree. Hao said: "I am willing to exchange my own life for the lives of a hundred thousand people."
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhedong transport grain passed below the city wall, Hao told the prefect to detain it. The prefect would not agree. Hao said, "I am willing to exchange my own life for the lives of a hundred thousand people."

sentences.zh: 」人感之切骨，號「洪佛子」。

translations.literal: The people were deeply moved and called him "Hong the Buddha-son."
translations.idiomatic: The people were deeply moved and called him "Hong the Buddha-son."

sentences.zh: 其後秀軍叛，縱掠郡民，無一得脫，惟過皓門曰：「此洪佛子家也。

translations.literal: Later the Xiuzhou garrison rebelled and plundered the people of the prefecture; none escaped except those who passed Hao's gate and said: "This is Hong the Buddha-son's house."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xiuzhou garrison rebelled and plundered the people of the prefecture. None escaped except those who passed Hao's gate and said, "This is Hong the Buddha-son's house."

sentences.zh: 」不敢犯。

translations.literal: They did not dare violate it.
translations.idiomatic: They did not dare violate it.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年五月，帝將如金陵，皓上書言：「內患甫平，外敵方熾，若輕至建康，恐金人乘虛侵軼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Jianyan the Emperor was about to go to Jinling; Hao memorialized: "Internal troubles have just been settled and foreign enemies are still fierce; if you lightly go to Jiankang, I fear the Jurchens will seize the opportunity to raid."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Jianyan the emperor was about to go to Jinling. Hao memorialized: "Internal troubles have just been settled and foreign enemies are still fierce. If you lightly go to Jiankang, I fear the Jurchens will seize the opportunity to raid."

sentences.zh: 宜先遣近臣往經營，俟告辦，回鑾未晚。

translations.literal: You should first send a close minister to make preparations; when all is reported ready, the imperial procession may return—not too late.
translations.idiomatic: You should first send a close minister to make preparations. When all is reported ready, the imperial procession may return—not too late.

sentences.zh: 」時朝議已定，不從，既而悔之。

translations.literal: " The court's deliberation was already settled and did not follow his advice; afterward they regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court's deliberation was already settled and did not follow his advice; afterward they regretted it.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝問宰輔近諫移蹕者謂誰，張浚以皓對。

translations.literal: Another day the Emperor asked the chief councillors who had recently remonstrated about moving the capital; Zhang Jun named Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor asked the chief councillors who had recently remonstrated about moving the capital; Zhang Jun named Hao.

sentences.zh: 時議遣使金國，浚又薦皓於呂頤浩，召與語，大悅。

translations.literal: When envoys to the Jin state were discussed, Jun again recommended Hao to Lü Yihao; he was summoned to speak and Yihao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys to the Jin state were discussed, Jun again recommended Hao to Lü Yihao. He was summoned to speak and Yihao was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 皓方居父喪，頤浩解衣巾，俾易墨衰絰入對。

translations.literal: Hao was then in mourning for his father; Yihao removed his cap and scarf and had him change from ink mourning dress to enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was then in mourning for his father. Yihao removed his cap and scarf and had him change from ink mourning dress to enter audience.

sentences.zh: 帝以國步艱難、兩宮遠播為憂。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved that the dynasty's fortunes were hard and the two palaces were far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved that the dynasty's fortunes were hard and the two palaces were far away.

sentences.zh: 皓極言：「天道好還，金人安能久陵中夏！

translations.literal: Hao spoke at length: "Heaven's way delights in return; how can the Jurchens long bully central China!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao spoke at length: "Heaven's way delights in return. How can the Jurchens long bully central China!"

sentences.zh: 此正春秋邲、郢之役，天其或者警晉訓楚也。

translations.literal: This is just like the battles of Bi and Ying in the Spring and Autumn—perhaps Heaven will warn Jin and instruct Chu."
translations.idiomatic: This is just like the battles of Bi and Ying in the Spring and Autumn—perhaps Heaven will warn Jin and instruct Chu."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，遷皓五官，擢徽猷閣待制，假禮部尚書，為大金通問使，龔璹副之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased, promoted Hao five ranks, made him Huixiu Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary, lent him the title of Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and made him Envoy for Communication to the Great Jin, with Gong Yu as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, promoted Hao five ranks, made him Huixiu Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary, lent him the title of Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and made him envoy for communication to the Great Jin, with Gong Yu as deputy.

sentences.zh: 令與執政議國書，皓欲有所易，頤浩不樂，遂抑遷官之命。

translations.literal: He was ordered to deliberate on the state letter with the chief councillors; Hao wished to change certain points and Yihao was displeased, and therefore suppressed the order promoting his rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to deliberate on the state letter with the chief councillors. Hao wished to change certain points and Yihao was displeased, and therefore suppressed the order promoting his rank.

sentences.zh: 時淮南盜賊踵起，李成甫就招，即命知泗州羈縻之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose one after another in Huainan; Li Cheng had just accepted recruitment and was appointed prefect of Sizhou to keep him in check.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits rose one after another in Huainan. Li Cheng had just accepted recruitment and was appointed prefect of Sizhou to keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 乃命皓兼淮南、京東等路撫諭使，俾成以所部衛皓至南京。

translations.literal: The court then appointed Hao concurrently Pacification Commissioner for Huainan, Jingdong, and other circuits, ordering Cheng to escort Hao with his troops to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The court then appointed Hao concurrently Pacification Commissioner for Huainan, Jingdong, and other circuits, ordering Cheng to escort Hao with his troops to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 比過淮南，成方與耿堅共圍楚州，責權州事賈敦詩以降敵，實持叛心。

translations.literal: When he passed Huainan, Cheng was then with Geng Jian jointly besieging Chuzhou, pressing Jia Dunshi, who held acting prefectural authority, to surrender to the enemy—he in fact harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed Huainan, Cheng was then with Geng Jian jointly besieging Chuzhou, pressing Jia Dunshi, who held acting prefectural authority, to surrender to the enemy—he in fact harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 皓先以書抵成，成以汴涸，虹有紅巾賊，軍食絕，不可往。

translations.literal: Hao first sent a letter to Cheng; Cheng said the Bian River was dry, Hong had red-turban bandits, and army provisions were cut off—he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hao first sent a letter to Cheng. Cheng said the Bian River was dry, Hong had red-turban bandits, and army provisions were cut off—he could not go.

sentences.zh: 皓聞堅起義兵，可撼以義，遣人密諭之曰：「君數千里赴國家急，山陽縱有罪，當禀命於朝；

translations.literal: Hao heard that Jian had raised righteous troops and could be moved by righteousness; he sent someone secretly to urge him: "You have come thousands of li in the state's urgent need; even if Shanyang is guilty, you should report to the court;"
translations.idiomatic: Hao heard that Jian had raised righteous troops and could be moved by righteousness. He sent someone secretly to urge him: "You have come thousands of li in the state's urgent need. Even if Shanyang is guilty, you should report to the court;"

sentences.zh: 今擅攻圍，名勤王，實作​​賊爾。

translations.literal: "now to attack and besiege on your own authority, your name is to aid the throne but in fact you are making yourself a bandit."
translations.idiomatic: "now to attack and besiege on your own authority, your name is to aid the throne but in fact you are making yourself a bandit."

sentences.zh: 」堅意動，遂強成斂兵。

translations.literal: " Jian was moved and therefore forced Cheng to withdraw his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was moved and therefore forced Cheng to withdraw his troops.

sentences.zh: 皓至泗境，迎騎介而來，龔璹曰：「虎口不可入。

translations.literal: When Hao reached the border of Si, welcoming horsemen came with weapons drawn; Gong Yu said: "A tiger's mouth cannot be entered."
translations.idiomatic: When Hao reached the border of Si, welcoming horsemen came with weapons drawn. Gong Yu said, "A tiger's mouth cannot be entered."

sentences.zh: 」皓遂還，上疏言：「成以朝廷饋餉不繼，有『引眾建康』之語。

translations.literal: Hao then returned and memorialized: "Cheng, because the court's provisions did not continue, has spoken of 'leading his host to Jiankang.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hao then returned and memorialized: "Cheng, because the court's provisions did not continue, has spoken of leading his host to Jiankang."

sentences.zh: 今靳賽據揚州，薛慶據高郵，萬一三叛連衡，何以待之？

translations.literal: "Now Jin Sai holds Yangzhou and Xue Qing holds Gaoyou—if by chance the three rebels join in alliance, how are we to deal with them?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now Jin Sai holds Yangzhou and Xue Qing holds Gaoyou—if by chance the three rebels join in alliance, how are we to deal with them?"

sentences.zh: 此含垢之時，宜使人諭意，優進官秩，畀之以京口綱運，如晉明帝待王敦可也。

translations.literal: "This is a time to swallow insults; someone should be sent to convey the court's intent, generously advance his rank, and give him the Jingkou transport assignment, as Mingdi of Jin treated Wang Dun."
translations.idiomatic: "This is a time to swallow insults. Someone should be sent to convey the court's intent, generously advance his rank, and give him the Jingkou transport assignment, as Mingdi of Jin treated Wang Dun."

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，帝即遣使撫成，給米伍萬石。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the Emperor immediately sent an envoy to pacify Cheng and gave him fifty thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted the emperor immediately sent an envoy to pacify Cheng and gave him fifty thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 頤浩惡其直達而不先白堂，奏皓託事稽留，貶二秩。

translations.literal: Yihao resented that he had reported directly without first informing the Secretariat and memorialized that Hao had delayed affairs on pretext; he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao resented that he had reported directly without first informing the Secretariat and memorialized that Hao had delayed affairs on pretext; he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 皓遂請出滁陽路，自壽春由東京以行。

translations.literal: Hao then asked to go out by the Chuyang route, traveling from Shouchun through the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then asked to go out by the Chuyang route, traveling from Shouchun through the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 至順昌，聞群盜李閻羅、小張俊者梗潁上道。

translations.literal: When he reached Shunchang he heard that the bandits Li Yanluo and Little Zhang Jun blocked the road on the Ying River.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shunchang he heard that the bandits Li Yanluo and Little Zhang Jun blocked the road on the Ying River.

sentences.zh: 皓與其黨遇，譬曉之曰：「自古無白頭賊。

translations.literal: Hao met their followers and admonished them: "Since antiquity there has never been a white-haired bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Hao met their followers and admonished them: "Since antiquity there has never been a white-haired bandit."

sentences.zh: 」其黨悔悟，皓使持書至賊巢，二渠魁聽命，領兵入宿衛。

translations.literal: His followers repented; Hao had them carry a letter to the bandits' lair, and the two chieftains obeyed and led their troops to enter palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: His followers repented. Hao had them carry a letter to the bandits' lair, and the two chieftains obeyed and led their troops to enter palace guard service.

sentences.zh: 皓至太原，留幾一年，金遇使人禮日薄。

translations.literal: When Hao reached Taiyuan he stayed nearly a year; the Jin's treatment of envoys grew daily thinner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao reached Taiyuan he stayed nearly a year; the Jin's treatment of envoys grew daily thinner.

sentences.zh: 及至雲中，粘罕迫二使仕劉豫，皓曰：「萬里銜命，不得奉兩宮南歸，恨力不能磔逆豫，忍事之邪！

translations.literal: When he reached Yunzhong, Nianhan pressed the two envoys to serve Liu Yu. Hao said: "I have carried commands ten thousand li and could not bring the two palaces south— I regret that my strength was not enough to dismember the rebel Yu; how could I endure to serve him!"
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yunzhong, Nianhan pressed the two envoys to serve Liu Yu. Hao said, "I have carried commands ten thousand li and could not bring the two palaces south. I regret that my strength was not enough to dismember the rebel Yu—how could I endure to serve him!"

sentences.zh: 留亦死，不即豫亦死，不願偷生鼠狗間，願就鼎鑊無悔。

translations.literal: "To remain is also death; not to serve Yu at once is also death. I do not wish to live like a rat or dog; I would rather enter the cauldron without regret."
translations.idiomatic: "To remain is also death; not to serve Yu at once is also death. I do not wish to live like a rat or dog. I would rather enter the cauldron without regret."

sentences.zh: 」粘罕怒，將殺之。

translations.literal: Nianhan was enraged and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan was enraged and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 旁一酋唶曰：「此真忠臣也。

translations.literal: A chieftain beside him cried: "This is a true loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: A chieftain beside him cried, "This is a true loyal minister!"

sentences.zh: 」目止劍士，為之跪請，得流遞冷山。

translations.literal: He stopped the swordsmen with his eyes and knelt to plead for him; Hao was sent by penal transport to Cold Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped the swordsmen with his eyes and knelt to plead for him. Hao was sent by penal transport to Cold Mountain.

sentences.zh: 流遞，猶編竄也。

translations.literal: Penal transport was still a form of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Penal transport was still a form of banishment.

sentences.zh: 惟璹至汴受豫官。

translations.literal: Only Yu went to Bian and accepted office under Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yu went to Bian and accepted office under Yu.

sentences.zh: 雲中至冷山行六十日，距金主所都僅百里，地苦寒，四月草生，八月已雪，穴居百家，陳王悟室聚落也。

translations.literal: From Yunzhong to Cold Mountain was a journey of sixty days, only a hundred li from where the Jin ruler dwelt; the land was bitterly cold—in the fourth month grass grew and by the eighth month there was already snow. A hundred households lived in caves; it was the settlement of Chen Wang Wushi.
translations.idiomatic: From Yunzhong to Cold Mountain was a journey of sixty days, only a hundred li from where the Jin ruler dwelt. The land was bitterly cold—in the fourth month grass grew and by the eighth month there was already snow. A hundred households lived in caves; it was the settlement of Chen Wang Wushi.

sentences.zh: 悟室敬皓，使教其八子。

translations.literal: Wushi respected Hao and had him teach his eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi respected Hao and had him teach his eight sons.

sentences.zh: 或二年不給食，盛夏衣粗布，嘗大雪薪盡，以馬矢然火煨麵食之。

translations.literal: Sometimes for two years they gave no food; in midsummer he wore coarse cloth; once when firewood was exhausted in great snow he used horse dung for fire to warm and eat noodles.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes for two years they gave no food. In midsummer he wore coarse cloth. Once when firewood was exhausted in great snow he used horse dung for fire to warm and eat noodles.

sentences.zh: 或獻取蜀策，悟室持問皓，皓力折之。

translations.literal: Someone presented a plan to take Shu; Wushi held it out and asked Hao, who forcefully refuted it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented a plan to take Shu. Wushi held it out and asked Hao, who forcefully refuted it.

sentences.zh: 悟室銳欲南侵，曰：「孰謂海大，我力可乾，但不能使天地相拍爾。

translations.literal: Wushi was keen to invade south and said: "Who says the sea is great? My strength can dry it up—I only cannot make heaven and earth strike each other."
translations.idiomatic: Wushi was keen to invade south and said, "Who says the sea is great? My strength can dry it up—I only cannot make heaven and earth strike each other."

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚，自古無四十年用兵不止者。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Warfare is like fire; if not checked it will burn itself out—since antiquity there has never been forty years of continuous warfare."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Warfare is like fire. If not checked it will burn itself out—since antiquity there has never been forty years of continuous warfare."

sentences.zh: 」又數為言所以來為兩國事，既不受使，乃令深入教小兒，非古者待使之禮也。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly spoke of why he had come—for the affairs of the two states; since they would not receive him as envoy, they had him go deep in to teach little children—this was not the ancient way of treating envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly spoke of why he had come—for the affairs of the two states. Since they would not receive him as envoy, they had him go deep in to teach little children—this was not the ancient way of treating envoys.

sentences.zh: 悟室或答或默，忽發怒曰：「汝作和事官，而口硬如許，謂我不能殺汝耶？

translations.literal: Wushi would answer or remain silent; suddenly he grew angry and said: "You are a peace commissioner, yet your mouth is this hard—do you think I cannot kill you?"
translations.idiomatic: Wushi would answer or remain silent. Suddenly he grew angry and said, "You are a peace commissioner, yet your mouth is this hard—do you think I cannot kill you?"

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「自分當死，顧大國無受殺行人之名，願投之水，以墜淵為名可也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "I have already resigned myself to death, but I fear the great state would bear the name of killing an envoy; I would rather be cast into the water so the abyss may be my name."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "I have already resigned myself to death, but I fear your great state would bear the name of killing an envoy. I would rather be cast into the water so the abyss may be my name."

sentences.zh: 」悟室義之而止。

translations.literal: Wushi admired his righteousness and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi admired his righteousness and stopped.

sentences.zh: 和議將成，悟室問所議十事，皓條析甚至。

translations.literal: When peace was about to be concluded, Wushi asked about the ten items under negotiation; Hao analyzed them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was about to be concluded, Wushi asked about the ten items under negotiation. Hao analyzed them in detail.

sentences.zh: 大略謂封冊乃虛名，年號本朝自有；

translations.literal: In general he said enfeoffment and investiture were empty names, and the reign title our dynasty already had its own;
translations.idiomatic: In general he said enfeoffment and investiture were empty names, and the reign title our dynasty already had its own;

sentences.zh: 金三千兩景德所無，東南不宜蠶，絹不可增也；

translations.literal: three thousand taels of gold the Jingde treaty never had; the southeast is unsuited to sericulture, and silk cannot be increased;
translations.idiomatic: three thousand taels of gold the Jingde treaty never had; the southeast is unsuited to sericulture, and silk cannot be increased;

sentences.zh: 至於取淮北人，景德載書猶可覆視。

translations.literal: as for taking people north of the Huai, the Jingde treaty documents can still be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: as for taking people north of the Huai, the Jingde treaty documents can still be consulted.

sentences.zh: 悟室曰：「誅投附人何為不可？

translations.literal: Wushi said: "Why can those who surrendered not be executed?"
translations.idiomatic: Wushi said, "Why can those who surrendered not be executed?"

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「昔魏侯景歸梁，梁武帝欲以易其侄蕭明於魏，景遂叛，陷臺城，中國決不蹈其覆轍。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Formerly when Marquis Jing of Wei returned to Liang, Emperor Wu of Liang wished to exchange him for his nephew Xiao Ming in Wei; Jing then rebelled, took Taicheng, and central China will certainly not tread that path again."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Formerly when Marquis Jing of Wei returned to Liang, Emperor Wu of Liang wished to exchange him for his nephew Xiao Ming in Wei. Jing then rebelled and took Taicheng—and central China will certainly not tread that path again."

sentences.zh: 」悟室悟曰：「汝性直不誑我，吾與汝如燕，遣汝歸議。

translations.literal: Wushi understood and said: "Your nature is straight and you do not deceive me; I will treat you like kin and send you back to deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: Wushi understood and said, "Your nature is straight and you do not deceive me. I will treat you like kin and send you back to deliberate."

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: He then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out.

sentences.zh: 會莫將北來，議不合，事復中止。

translations.literal: When Mo Jiang came north to negotiate, the talks did not agree and the matter again stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Jiang came north to negotiate, the talks did not agree and the matter again stopped.

sentences.zh: 留燕甫一月，兀术殺悟室，黨類株連者數千人，獨皓與異論幾死，故得免。

translations.literal: He had stayed in Yan only a month when Wuzhu killed Wushi; thousands in his faction were implicated, but Hao alone, because of his dissenting views, nearly died and therefore was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He had stayed in Yan only a month when Wuzhu killed Wushi. Thousands in his faction were implicated, but Hao alone, because of his dissenting views, nearly died and therefore was spared.

sentences.zh: 方二帝遷居五國城，皓在雲中密遣人奏書，以桃、梨、粟面獻，二帝始知帝即位。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were moved to the Five States City, Hao in Yunzhong secretly sent men to memorialize, presenting peaches, pears, and millet flour—the two emperors then learned that the Emperor had ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors were moved to the Five States City, Hao in Yunzhong secretly sent men to memorialize, presenting peaches, pears, and millet flour—the two emperors then learned that the emperor had ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 皓聞祐陵訃，北向泣血，旦夕臨，諱日操文以祭，其辭激烈，舊臣讀之皆揮涕。

translations.literal: When Hao heard the mourning news for Youling he wept blood facing north, attended morning and evening, and on the anniversary composed a text to sacrifice; its wording was fierce, and old ministers who read it all wiped away tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao heard the mourning news for Youling he wept blood facing north, attended morning and evening, and on the anniversary composed a text to sacrifice. Its wording was fierce, and old ministers who read it all wiped away tears.

sentences.zh: 紹興十年，因諜者趙德，書機事數万言，藏故絮中，歸達於帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shaoxing, through the spy Zhao De, he wrote several tens of thousands of words on military affairs, hid them in old cotton padding, and they reached the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Shaoxing, through the spy Zhao De, he wrote several tens of thousands of words on military affairs, hid them in old cotton padding, and they reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 言：「順昌之役，金人震懼奪魄，燕山珍寶盡徙以北，意欲捐燕以南棄之。

translations.literal: He said: "In the battle of Shunchang the Jurchens were shaken and lost their souls; treasures of Yanshan were all moved north—they intend to abandon everything south of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "In the battle of Shunchang the Jurchens were shaken and lost their souls. Treasures of Yanshan were all moved north—they intend to abandon everything south of Yan."

sentences.zh: 王師亟還，自失機會，今再舉尚可。

translations.literal: "Our army returned in haste and lost the opportunity; if we strike again now it can still be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Our army returned in haste and lost the opportunity. If we strike again now it can still be done."

sentences.zh: 」十一年，又求得太后書，遣李微持歸，帝大喜曰：「朕不知太后寧否幾二十年，雖遣使百輩，不如此一書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he also obtained a letter from the Grand Empress Dowager and sent Li Wei to carry it back; the Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "I have not known whether the Grand Empress Dowager was safe for nearly twenty years; though I have sent envoys a hundred times, none equals this one letter."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he also obtained a letter from the Grand Empress Dowager and sent Li Wei to carry it back. The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "I have not known whether the Grand Empress Dowager was safe for nearly twenty years. Though I have sent envoys a hundred times, none equals this one letter."

sentences.zh: 」是冬，又密奏書曰：「金已厭兵，勢不能久，異時以婦女隨軍，今不敢也。

translations.literal: That winter he again sent a secret memorial: "The Jin are already weary of warfare and cannot last long; formerly they took women with the army, now they dare not."
translations.idiomatic: That winter he again sent a secret memorial: "The Jin are already weary of warfare and cannot last long. Formerly they took women with the army; now they dare not."

sentences.zh: 若和議未決，不若乘勢進擊，再造反掌爾。

translations.literal: "If peace is not yet settled, it would be better to strike while the momentum is favorable—restoration would be as easy as turning the hand."
translations.idiomatic: "If peace is not yet settled, it would be better to strike while the momentum is favorable—restoration would be as easy as turning the hand."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「胡銓封事此或有之，金人知中國有人，益懼。

translations.literal: He also said: "Hu Quan's sealed memorial may exist; the Jurchens know there are men in China and fear all the more."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Hu Quan's sealed memorial may exist. The Jurchens know there are men in China and fear all the more."

sentences.zh: 張丞相名動異域，惜置之散地。

translations.literal: "Chief Councillor Zhang's name shakes foreign lands—it is a pity he is placed in an idle post."
translations.idiomatic: "Chief Councillor Zhang's name shakes foreign lands—it is a pity he is placed in an idle post."

sentences.zh: 」又問李綱、趙鼎安否，獻六朝御容、徽宗御書。

translations.literal: He also asked whether Li Gang and Zhao Ding were well, and presented the imperial portraits of the Six Dynasties and Emperor Huizong's calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked whether Li Gang and Zhao Ding were well, and presented the imperial portraits of the Six Dynasties and Emperor Huizong's calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 其後梓宮及太后歸音，皓皆先報。

translations.literal: Afterward, when news came of the return of the imperial coffin and the Grand Empress Dowager, Hao reported all of it first.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when news came of the return of the imperial coffin and the Grand Empress Dowager, Hao reported all of it first.

sentences.zh: 初，皓至燕，宇文虛中已受金官，因薦皓。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao arrived in Yan, Yuwen Xuzhong had already accepted Jin office and thereupon recommended Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao first reached Yan, Yuwen Xuzhong had already taken office under the Jin and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 金主聞其名，欲以為翰林直學士，力辭之。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler heard his name and wished to appoint him Hanlin Direct Academician; he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler heard of him and wished to make him Hanlin Direct Academician, but Hao firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 皓有逃歸意，乃請於參政韓昉，乞於真定或大名以自養。

translations.literal: Hao had thoughts of escaping to return home and so petitioned Administrative Assistant Han Fang, begging to support himself at Zhending or Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wanted to flee south and petitioned Administrative Assistant Han Fang, asking to live quietly at Zhending or Daming.

sentences.zh: 昉怒，始易皓官為中京副留守，再降為留司判官。

translations.literal: Fang was angry; he first changed Hao's office to Vice Commissioner of Zhongjing, then demoted him again to Remaining Office Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was furious. He first reassigned Hao as Vice Commissioner of Zhongjing, then demoted him again to Remaining Office Aide.

sentences.zh: 趣行屢矣，皓乞不就職，昉竟不能屈。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly urged to proceed, but Hao begged not to take office, and Fang ultimately could not break him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pressed him repeatedly to take up the post, but Hao refused, and in the end Fang could not force him to yield.

sentences.zh: 金法，雖未易官而曾經任使者，永不可歸，昉遂令皓校雲中進士試，蓋欲以計墮皓也。

translations.literal: Under Jin law, even if one had not changed office, once one had previously served as envoy one could never return; Fang therefore had Hao proofread the Yunzhong metropolitan examination, presumably intending by this stratagem to ruin Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin law, anyone who had once served as an envoy could never go home, even if he had not formally changed office. Fang therefore had Hao proofread the Yunzhong metropolitan examination—a scheme meant to trap him.

sentences.zh: 皓復以疾辭。

translations.literal: Hao again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Hao again pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金主以生子大赦，許使人還鄉，皓與張邵、朱弁三人在遣中。

translations.literal: Before long, the Jin ruler granted a general amnesty on account of the birth of a son and permitted envoys to return home; Hao, Zhang Shao, and Zhu Bian were the three among those dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, the Jin ruler proclaimed a general amnesty for the birth of a son and allowed envoys to return home. Hao, Zhang Shao, and Zhu Bian were among those sent back.

sentences.zh: 金人懼為患，猶遣人追之，七騎及淮，而皓已登舟。

translations.literal: The Jurchens, fearing trouble, still sent men to pursue them; seven riders reached the Huai, but Hao had already boarded a boat.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing trouble, the Jurchens still sent pursuers after them. Seven riders reached the Huai just as Hao had already boarded a boat.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，見於內殿，力求郡養母。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year, he had an audience in the inner hall and earnestly sought a prefecture with which to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year of Shaoxing, he had an audience in the inner hall and earnestly asked for a prefectural post so he could support his mother.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿忠貫日月，志不忘君，雖蘇武不能過，豈可舍朕去邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your loyalty pierces sun and moon; your will never forget your sovereign—even Su Wu could not surpass you. How could you leave Us!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your loyalty shines like sun and moon; your heart never forgets your sovereign. Even Su Wu could not surpass you—how could you leave me!"

sentences.zh: 」請見慈寧宮，帟人設簾，太后曰：「吾故識尚書。

translations.literal: He requested an audience at Cining Palace; the attendants set up a screen, and the Grand Empress Dowager said: "I already recognize the Former Minister."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to see the Grand Empress Dowager at Cining Palace. Attendants hung a curtain, but the empress dowager said, "I already know the Former Minister."

sentences.zh: 」命撤之。

translations.literal: She ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the curtain taken down.

sentences.zh: 皓自建炎己酉出使，至是還，留北中凡十五年。

translations.literal: Hao had gone out as envoy in the jiyou year of Jianyan; now he returned, having remained in the north altogether fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had been sent abroad in the jiyou year of Jianyan; now he returned after fifteen years in the north.

sentences.zh: 同時使者十三人，惟皓、邵、弁得生還，而忠義之聲聞於天下者，獨皓而已。

translations.literal: Of the thirteen envoys at the same time, only Hao, Shao, and Bian returned alive; yet of those whose fame for loyalty and righteousness resounded through the realm, Hao alone.
translations.idiomatic: Of the thirteen envoys sent at the same time, only Hao, Shao, and Bian returned alive—but of those whose name for loyalty and righteousness resounded through the realm, Hao alone stood apart.

sentences.zh: 皓既對，退見秦檜，語連日不止，曰：「張和公金人所憚，乃不得用。
