translations.literal: After Hao had been received in audience, he withdrew and saw Qin Hui, speaking without cease for days on end, saying: "Lord He of Zhang is what the Jurchens fear, yet he is not employed."
translations.idiomatic: After his audience, Hao withdrew and saw Qin Hui, talking for days without stopping. He said, "Zhang Jun is the man the Jurchens fear, yet he is not used."

sentences.zh: 錢塘暫居，而景靈宮、太廟皆極土木之華，豈非示無中原意乎？

translations.literal: Temporary residence at Qiantang, while Jingling Shrine and the Imperial Ancestral Temple are both built to the utmost splendor of earth and timber—is this not showing that there is no intent toward the Central Plains?
translations.idiomatic: The court dwells temporarily at Qiantang while Jingling Shrine and the Imperial Ancestral Temple are built to lavish splendor—is this not a sign that there is no will to recover the Central Plains?

sentences.zh: 」檜不懌，謂皓子适曰：「尊公信有忠節，得上眷。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was displeased and said to Hao's son Shi: "Your honored father truly has loyalty and integrity and has won the sovereign's favor."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was displeased and said to Hong Hao's son Hong Shi, "Your honored father truly has loyalty and integrity, and has won the emperor's favor."

sentences.zh: 但官職如讀書，速則易終而無味，須如黃鐘、大呂乃可。

translations.literal: But office is like reading: if too fast it ends easily and lacks savor; one must be like the Yellow Bell and Great Lu tones.
translations.idiomatic: But office is like reading a book: if you rush through it, it ends too quickly and leaves no lasting savor. One must advance slowly, like the Yellow Bell and Great Lu tones.

sentences.zh: 」八月，除徽猷閣直學士、提舉萬壽觀兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion, Director of the Wanshou Abbey, and concurrently Acting Director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion, Director of the Wanshou Abbey, and concurrently Acting Director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 金人來取趙彬等三十人家屬，詔歸之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens came to take the families of Zhao Bin and thirty others; an edict ordered them returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens came to reclaim the families of Zhao Bin and thirty others, and an edict ordered that they be sent back.

sentences.zh: 皓曰：「昔韓起謁環於鄭，鄭，小國也，能引義不與。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Formerly Han Qi sought an audience with Huan at Zheng; Zheng was a small state, yet it could uphold righteousness and refuse to surrender him."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Long ago Han Qi sought an audience with Huan at Zheng. Zheng was a small state, yet it upheld righteousness and refused to hand him over."

sentences.zh: 金既限淮，官屬皆吳人，宜留不遣，蓋慮知其虛實也。

translations.literal: The Jin is now bounded by the Huai; their officials are all men of Wu and ought to be kept and not sent back—for they surely fear we know their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin is now bounded by the Huai, and these officials are all men of Wu. We ought to keep them and not send them back, for the Jin surely fear that we will learn their true strength and weakness.

sentences.zh: 彼方困於蒙兀，姑示強以嘗中國，若遽從之，謂秦無人，益輕我矣。

translations.literal: They are just then hard pressed by the Mongols and are for the moment showing strength to test China; if we hastily comply, they will say Qin has no men and slight us all the more.
translations.idiomatic: They are hard pressed by the Mongols and are only putting on a show of strength to test China. If we comply at once, they will say there is no one left in Qin's court and despise us all the more."

sentences.zh: 」檜變色曰：「公無謂秦無人。

translations.literal: Qin Hui changed color and said: "Sir, do not say Qin has no men."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui's face changed and he said, "Sir, do not say there is no one in Qin's court."

sentences.zh: 」既而復上疏曰：「恐以不與之故，或致渝盟，宜告之曰：『俟淵聖及皇族歸，乃遣。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again submitted a memorial: "I fear that for refusal we may break the alliance; we should tell them: 'Wait until the Former Emperor and the imperial clan return, then we will send them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted another memorial: "I fear that refusal may rupture the alliance. We should tell them, 'Wait until the Former Emperor and the imperial clan return, and then we will send them back.'"

sentences.zh: 』」又言：「王倫、郭元邁以身徇國，棄之不取，緩急何以使人？

translations.literal: He also said: "Wang Lun and Guo Yuanmai gave their bodies for the state; to abandon them and not retrieve them—when urgency comes, how can we send men?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wang Lun and Guo Yuanmai gave their lives for the state. If we abandon them and do not bring them home, how can we expect anyone to serve as envoy when the need is urgent?"

sentences.zh: 」檜大怒，又因言室撚寄聲，檜怒益甚，語在《檜傳》。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was greatly enraged; moreover because of words about Shi Nian relaying messages, Qin Hui's anger grew all the sharper—the account is in the Biography of Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was furious, and grew even angrier when Hao spoke of messages relayed by Shi Nian. The full account is given in the Biography of Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 翌日，侍御史李文會劾皓不省母，出知饒州。

translations.literal: The next day, Supervising Censor Li Wenhui impeached Hao for failing to care for his mother; he was removed and made prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Supervising Censor Li Wenhui impeached Hao for neglecting his mother, and he was sent out as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，大水，中官白鍔宣言：「燮理乖盭，洪尚書名聞天下，胡不用？

translations.literal: The next year there was a great flood; the palace eunuch Bai E proclaimed: "The harmonizing of governance is out of tune—Minister Hong's name is known throughout the realm; why is he not employed?"
translations.idiomatic: The next year there was a great flood, and the palace eunuch Bai E declared publicly, "The government is out of harmony, and Minister Hong's name is known throughout the realm—why is he not used?"

sentences.zh: 」檜聞之愈怒，系鍔大理獄，尋流嶺表。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui heard this he grew angrier still, imprisoned E in the Court of Judicial Review, and soon exiled him beyond the Lingnan passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui heard this he grew even angrier. He had Bai E imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review and soon exiled him beyond the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 諫官詹大方遂論皓與鍔為刎頸交，更相稱譽，罷皓提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Zhan Dafa then charged that Hao and E were sworn friends who mutually praised each other; Hao was dismissed from his directorship of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Zhan Dafa then charged that Hao and Bai E were sworn friends who praised each other in turn, and Hao was dismissed from his directorship of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鍔初不識皓，特以從太后北歸，在金國素知皓名爾。

translations.literal: E had not known Hao at first; it was only because, returning south with the Grand Empress Dowager, he had long known Hao's name in the Jin state.
translations.idiomatic: Bai E had not known Hao at first; he had only heard of Hao's name in the Jin state because he had returned south with the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 尋居母喪，他言者猶謂皓睥睨鈞衡。

translations.literal: Before long he observed mourning for his mother; other critics still said Hao cast a sidelong eye at the scales of power.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his mother, yet other critics still claimed that Hao was casting a covetous eye on high office.

sentences.zh: 終喪，除饒州通判。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Vice Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Vice Prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 李勤又附檜誣皓作欺世飛語，責濠州團練副使，安置英州。

translations.literal: Li Qin again siding with Qin Hui slandered Hao for composing deceitful slanders of the world; he was reduced to Regiment Vice Commander of Haozhou and settled at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qin, again siding with Qin Hui, slandered Hao for spreading deceitful rumors; Hao was reduced to Regiment Vice Commander of Haozhou and settled at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 居九年，始復朝奉郎，徙袁州，至南雄州卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: After nine years' residence he was at last restored to Court Gentleman for Appeasement, transferred to Yuanzhou, and died reaching Nanxiong Prefecture at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years there he was at last restored to Court Gentleman for Appeasement and transferred to Yuanzhou, but died on the road at Nanxiong Prefecture at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 死後一日，檜亦死。

translations.literal: One day after his death, Qin Hui also died.
translations.idiomatic: One day after Hao's death, Qin Hui also died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞皓卒，嗟惜之，复敷文閣直學士，贈四官。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of Hao's death he sighed in regret, restored him as Direct Academician of the Fujun Pavilion, and posthumously promoted him four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Hao had died, he sighed in regret, restored him as Direct Academician of the Fujun Pavilion, and posthumously promoted him four ranks.

sentences.zh: 久之，复徽猷閣直學士，諡忠宣。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again restored as Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion, with the posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again restored as Direct Academician of the Huayou Pavilion and given the posthumous title Zhongxuan, "Loyal and Proclaiming."

sentences.zh: 皓雖久在北廷，不堪其苦，然為金人所敬，所著詩文，爭鈔誦求鋟梓。

translations.literal: Though Hao long endured the northern court and could not bear its hardships, he was honored by the Jurchens; his poems and essays were eagerly copied, recited, and sought for printing.
translations.idiomatic: Although Hao had long suffered in the northern court and could hardly bear the hardship, the Jurchens respected him. People competed to copy, recite, and print his poems and essays.

sentences.zh: 既歸，後使者至，必問皓為何官、居何地。

translations.literal: After he returned, whenever later envoys arrived they invariably asked what office Hao held and where he dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, whenever later envoys arrived they always asked what office Hao held and where he lived.

sentences.zh: 性急義，當艱危中不少變。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick to righteousness and did not waver in the slightest amid hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was quick to act on principle and did not waver in the slightest amid hardship and danger.

sentences.zh: 懿節后之戚趙伯璘隸悟室戲下，貧甚，皓賙之。

translations.literal: Zhao Bolin, a kinsman of Empress Yijie, was under Wushi's command and was extremely poor; Hao relieved him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bolin, a kinsman of Empress Yijie, served under Wushi and was desperately poor; Hao gave him relief.

sentences.zh: 范鎮之孫祖平為傭奴，皓言於金人而釋之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen's grandson Zuping was a hired slave; Hao spoke to the Jurchens and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen's grandson Zuping had been reduced to hired servitude; Hao spoke to the Jurchens and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 劉光世庶女為人豢豕，贖而嫁之。

translations.literal: A concubine-born daughter of Liu Guangshi was kept by someone who raised pigs; he redeemed her and gave her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine-born daughter of Liu Guangshi had been kept by a man who raised pigs; Hao redeemed her and saw her married.

sentences.zh: 他貴族流落賤微者，皆力拔以出。

translations.literal: Other nobles who had fallen to low and humble stations—he all exerted himself to lift out.
translations.idiomatic: For other nobles who had fallen into low and wretched circumstances, he exerted himself to pull them out.

sentences.zh: 惟為檜所嫉，不死於敵國，乃死於讒慝。

translations.literal: Only because Qin Hui envied him, he did not die in the enemy state but died from slander and malice.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Qin Hui envied him, he did not die in the enemy state but perished from slander and malice.

sentences.zh: 皓博學強記，有文集五十卷及《帝王勇要》、《姓氏指南》、《松漠紀聞》、《金國文具錄》等書。

translations.literal: Hao was broadly learned with a powerful memory; he had a collected writings in fifty juan and books such as Essentials of the Emperor's Courage, Guide to Surnames, Record of the Pine Desert, and Record of Jin State Documents and Implements.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was broadly learned with a powerful memory. He left a collected writings in fifty juan, as well as books including Essentials of Imperial Valor, Guide to Surnames, Record of the Pine Desert, and Record of Jin Documents and Implements.

sentences.zh: 子适、遵、邁。

translations.literal: His sons were Shi, Zun, and Mai.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shi, Zun, and Mai.

sentences.zh: 子 适

translations.literal: Son: Shi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shi

sentences.zh: 适字景伯，皓長子也。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Jingbo, was Hao's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Shi, styled Jingbo, was Hong Hao's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟，日誦三千言。

translations.literal: As a child he was quick and perceptive, reciting three thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was exceptionally bright and could recite three thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 皓使朔方，适年甫十三，能任家事。

translations.literal: When Hao went as envoy to the northern frontier, Shi was just thirteen and could manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Hao went as envoy to the north, Shi was only thirteen but already able to manage the household.

sentences.zh: 以皓出使恩，補修職郎。

translations.literal: Through the grace of Hao's ambassadorial service he was appointed Supplementary Xiuzhi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Through the grace of his father's ambassadorial service he was appointed Supplementary Xiuzhi Lang.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年，與弟遵同中博學宏詞科。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing he and his younger brother Zun together passed the Erudite and Literary Grand Speech examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing he and his younger brother Hong Zun both passed the Erudite and Literary Grand Speech examination.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「父在遠方，子能自立，此忠義報也，宜升擢。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "The father is in a distant land; the sons can stand on their own—this is a return of loyalty and righteousness; they should be promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "Their father is far away, yet the sons can stand on their own. This is loyalty and righteousness rewarded—they should be promoted."

sentences.zh: 」遂除敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Collator at the Statutes and Decrees Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was thereupon appointed Collator at the Statutes and Decrees Office.

sentences.zh: 後三年，弟邁亦中是選，由是三洪文名滿天下。

translations.literal: Three years later his younger brother Mai also passed this selection; thereby the literary fame of the three Hongs filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later his younger brother Mai also passed the same examination, and the literary fame of the three Hongs filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He was changed to Corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甫數月，皓歸，忤秦檜，出知饒州，适亦出為台州通判。

translations.literal: Only a few months later, Hao returned, offended Qin Hui, and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou; Shi also was sent out as Vice Prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few months later Hong Hao returned, offended Qin Hui, and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou; Shi was also sent out as Vice Prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 垂滿，皓謫英州，适复論罷，往來嶺南省侍者九載。

translations.literal: When his term was nearly finished, Hao was demoted to Yingzhou; Shi was again impeached and dismissed, traveling back and forth to Lingnan to attend his father for nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of his term, Hong Hao was demoted to Yingzhou and Shi was again impeached and dismissed. For nine years he traveled back and forth to Lingnan to attend his father.

sentences.zh: 檜死皓還，道卒，服闋，起知荊門軍。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, Hao returned but died on the road; when mourning ended Shi was raised to administer Jingmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui died, Hong Hao started home but died on the road. After mourning ended, Shi was appointed to administer Jingmen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 應詔上寬卹四事：輕茶額錢，它州代貢禮物，辟試闈以復舊額，蠲官田令不種者輸租。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he submitted four items of lenient relief: reducing the tea quota levy, having other prefectures submit tribute goods in place, reopening examination halls to restore former quotas, and remitting official fields so those who did not plant need not pay rent.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an edict he submitted four proposals for lenient relief: reducing the tea quota levy, having other prefectures submit tribute goods in lieu, reopening examination halls to restore former quotas, and remitting rent on official fields for those who had not planted them.

sentences.zh: 改知徽州，尋提舉江東路常平茶鹽，首言役法不均之弊。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Huizhou; soon he was appointed Commissioner of Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt on the Jiangdong Circuit, first speaking of the evils of unequal levy of labor obligations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Huizhou, and soon appointed Commissioner of Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt on the Jiangdong Circuit, where he first spoke of the evils of unequal labor levies.

sentences.zh: 會完顏亮來侵，上親征，适覲金陵，言：「本路旱，百姓逐食於淮，复遭金兵，今各懷歸而田產為官鬻，請聽其估贖之。

translations.literal: When Wanyan Liang came to invade, the Emperor personally campaigned; Shi had an audience at Jinling and said: "This circuit has drought; the people went to the Huai for food and again met Jin troops; now each wishes to return while their fields and property have been sold by the government—please allow them to redeem at assessed value."
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Liang invaded and the emperor personally took the field, Shi had an audience at Jinling and said, "This circuit has suffered drought. The people went to the Huai for food and then met Jin troops again. Now they all wish to return, but their fields and property have been sold by the government. Please allow them to redeem them at assessed value."

sentences.zh: 」及亮斃，适上疏曰：「大定僭號，諸國未必服從，宜多遣密詔傳諭中原義士，各取州縣，因以畀之。

translations.literal: When Liang died, Shi submitted a memorial: "Da Ding usurps the title; the various states may not necessarily submit; we should send many secret edicts to proclaim to loyalists of the Central Plains, each to take prefectures and counties, and then grant them those territories."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang died, Shi submitted a memorial: "Da Ding has usurped the throne, and the various states may not submit to him. We should send many secret edicts to rally loyalists in the Central Plains, let each take prefectures and counties, and then grant those territories to them."

sentences.zh: 王師但留屯淮、泗，募兵積粟，以為聲援。

translations.literal: Our imperial army need only remain encamped at Huai and Si, recruit troops and accumulate grain, to serve as vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: Our imperial army need only remain encamped at Huai and Si, recruiting troops and accumulating grain to serve as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 俟蜀、漢、山東之兵數道皆集，見可而進，庶幾兵力不頓，可以萬全。

translations.literal: Wait until armies from Shu, Han, and Shandong gather on several routes; advance when opportunity appears—then perhaps military strength will not stall and complete safety can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until armies from Shu, Han, and Shandong gather on several routes, then advance when the moment is right. In that way our forces will not be exhausted and the campaign may be made fully secure."

sentences.zh: 」升尚書戶部郎中，總領淮東軍馬錢糧。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue of the Department of State Affairs and overall director of military horses, funds, and grain in Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and put in overall charge of military horses, funds, and grain in Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，海州解圍，符離用兵，饋餉繁夥，适究心調度，供億無闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Haizhou was relieved from siege and troops were deployed at Fuli; supplies were numerous and complex—Shi devoted himself to coordination and provision, and nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Haizhou was relieved from siege and troops were deployed at Fuli. Supplies were numerous and complex, but Shi devoted himself to coordination and nothing was lacking.

sentences.zh: 遷司農少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年二月，召貳太常兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Longxing he was summoned as Deputy of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Acting Director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Longxing he was summoned as Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Acting Director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 上欲除諸將環衛官，詔討論其制。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to appoint the various generals to Palace Guard offices and ordered discussion of the institution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint the various generals to Palace Guard offices and ordered a discussion of the institution.

sentences.zh: 适具唐及本朝沿革十一條上之，且言：「太祖、太宗朝，常以處諸將及降王之君臣，自後多以皇族為之，故國史以為官存而事廢。

translations.literal: Shi set forth eleven articles on the evolution under Tang and our dynasty and submitted them, saying: "In the reigns of Taizu and Taizong, these offices were commonly used to place generals and the ministers and subjects of surrendered kings; afterward they were mostly filled by imperial clansmen, so the national history holds that the offices existed while their functions were abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Shi set forth eleven articles on the evolution of the institution under Tang and our dynasty and submitted them, saying, "In the reigns of Taizu and Taizong, these offices were commonly used to place generals and the ministers and subjects of surrendered kings. Later they were mostly filled by imperial clansmen, so the national history says the offices survived while their functions were abandoned."

sentences.zh: 陛下修飭戎備，不必遠取唐制，祖宗故事蓋可法則。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is repairing military readiness; there is no need to reach far for Tang institutions—the precedents of our ancestors can serve as models.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is strengthening military readiness. There is no need to reach back to Tang institutions—the precedents of our ancestors can serve as models.

sentences.zh: 今徑行換授，恐有減奉之患，乞如閣職兼帶節度，至刺史帶上將軍，橫行遙郡帶大將軍，正使帶將軍，副使帶中郎將，又以下則帶左右郎將，其官府人吏，令有司相度以聞。

translations.literal: If we now directly transfer and appoint, I fear there will be the harm of reduced stipends; I beg that like pavilion posts one concurrently bear regimental commands—from Inspector up to General-in-Chief, Tranverse Commissioner of Remote Prefectures to Grand General, Chief Commissioner to General, Vice Commissioner to Major-General, and below that to Colonel of the Left and Right—their office staff and clerks should be measured by the relevant offices and reported.
translations.idiomatic: If we now directly transfer and appoint them, I fear there will be the harm of reduced stipends. I beg that, as with pavilion posts, they concurrently bear military titles: Inspectors up to General-in-Chief, Tranverse Commissioners of Remote Prefectures to Grand General, Chief Commissioners to General, Vice Commissioners to Major-General, and below that to Colonels of the Left and Right. As for their office staff and clerks, let the relevant offices measure the matter and report."

sentences.zh: 」除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時金人再犯淮，羽檄沓至，書詔填委，諮訪酬答率稱上旨，自此有大用意。

translations.literal: At the time the Jurchens again violated the Huai; urgent dispatches piled up, documents and edicts overflowed; consultations and replies all accorded with the Emperor's intent—from this he came under great regard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jurchens again violated the Huai. Urgent dispatches piled up and documents and edicts overflowed his desk, yet his consultations and replies all accorded with the emperor's intent, and from this he came under great regard.

sentences.zh: 金既尋盟，首為賀生辰使。

translations.literal: Once the Jin soon renewed the alliance, he was first appointed envoy to congratulate on the birthday.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin soon renewed the alliance, he was first appointed envoy to congratulate them on the emperor's birthday.

sentences.zh: 金遣同簽書樞密院事高嗣先接伴，自言其父司空有德於皓，相與甚歡，得其要領以歸。

translations.literal: The Jin sent Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs Gao Sixian as reception envoy; he himself said his father Sikong had shown kindness to Hao; they got on very well and Shi returned grasping their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs Gao Sixian as reception envoy. Gao said his father Sikong had shown kindness to Hong Hao, and the two got on very well. Shi returned having grasped their essentials.

sentences.zh: 六月，除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Academician of the Duandian Hall and Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Academician of the Duandian Hall and Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上諭參政錢端禮、虞允文曰：「三省事與洪适商量。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Administrative Assistants Qian Duanli and Yu Yunwen: "Affairs of the Three Departments are to be deliberated with Hong Shi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Administrative Assistants Qian Duanli and Yu Yunwen, "Affairs of the Three Departments are to be deliberated with Hong Shi."

sentences.zh: 」東西府始同班奏事。

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western bureaus for the first time jointly attended court to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern and Western bureaus for the first time jointly attended court to report affairs.

sentences.zh: 八月，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫林安宅以銅錢多入北境，請禁之，即蜀中取鐵錢行之淮上。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Petition Grandee Lin Anzhai, because much copper coin flowed into the northern frontier, requested it be banned and iron coin be taken from Shu for circulation on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Petition Grandee Lin Anzhai, noting that much copper coin was flowing into the northern frontier, requested that it be banned and that iron coin be taken from Shu for circulation on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 事既行，适言其不可。

translations.literal: Once the measure was implemented, Shi said it was not feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Once the measure was implemented, Shi said it would not work.

sentences.zh: 上問之，适曰：「今每州不得千緡，一州以萬戶計之，每家才得數百，恐民間無以貿易。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked him; Shi said: "Now each prefecture receives no more than a thousand strings; calculating for a prefecture of ten thousand households, each household gets only a few hundred—I fear the people will have nothing with which to trade."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him about it, and Shi said, "Now each prefecture receives no more than a thousand strings. For a prefecture of ten thousand households, each household gets only a few hundred. I fear the people will have nothing with which to trade."

sentences.zh: 且客旅無回貨，鹽場有大利害。

translations.literal: Moreover travelers will have no return goods; the salt fields have great stakes involved.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover travelers will have no return goods to carry, and the salt fields have great stakes involved.

sentences.zh: 」上以為然，乃寢前命，但於蜀中取十五萬緡，行之廬、和二州而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this right; the prior order was then shelved, and only a hundred and fifty thousand strings were taken from Shu for circulation in Lu and He prefectures alone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, shelved the earlier order, and took only a hundred and fifty thousand strings from Shu for circulation in Lu and He prefectures alone.

sentences.zh: 十二月，拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，春霖，适引咎乞退，林安宅抗疏論适，既而臺臣復合奏。

translations.literal: Before long, spring rains continued; Shi accepted blame and begged to retire; Lin Anzhai submitted a protesting memorial against Shi, and soon censorial officials jointly memorialized again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, prolonged spring rains fell. Shi accepted blame and asked to retire. Lin Anzhai submitted a protesting memorial against him, and soon the censorial officials jointly memorialized again.

sentences.zh: 三月，除觀文殿學士、提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed Academician of the Guanwen Hall and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was appointed Academician of the Guanwen Hall and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋起知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to administer Shaoxing Prefecture and serve as Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was raised to administer Shaoxing Prefecture and serve as Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 再奉祠。

translations.literal: He again received a sacrificial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He again received a sacrificial appointment.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十一年薨，年六十八，諡文惠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chunxi he died at age sixty-eight; his posthumous title was Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chunxi he died at the age of sixty-eight and was given the posthumous title Wenhui, "Literary and Beneficent."

sentences.zh: 适以文學聞望，遭時遇主，自兩制一月入政府，又四閱月居相位，又三月罷政，然無大建明以究其學。

translations.literal: Shi was known for literary learning and reputation; encountering the age and meeting his sovereign, from the Two Drafting Offices he entered the government in one month, held the chief ministership for four months, and resigned after three months—yet he had no great constructive proposals to exhaust his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was known for literary learning and reputation. Meeting the times and finding favor with his sovereign, he entered the government from the Two Drafting Offices within a month, held the chief ministership for four months, and resigned after three more—yet he had no great constructive proposals by which to fully apply his learning.

sentences.zh: 家居十有六年，兄弟鼎立，子孫森然，以著述吟詠自樂，近世備福鮮有及之。

translations.literal: At home for sixteen years, his brothers stood like a tripod, his descendants numerous; he took delight in writing and poetic composition—in recent times few have enjoyed such complete felicity.
translations.idiomatic: At home for sixteen years, his brothers stood like a tripod and his descendants were numerous. He took delight in writing and poetry, and in recent times few have enjoyed such complete felicity.

sentences.zh: 或謂适黨湯思退，又謂适來自淮東，言張浚妄費，浚以此罷相，子九人：槻、柲、槢、𣘀、樌、桴、楹、槺、梠。

translations.literal: Some said Shi was partisan to Tang Situi; others said Shi, coming from Huaidong, spoke of Zhang Jun's reckless expenditure, and Jun was dismissed as chief councillor for this; he had nine sons: Gui, Bi, Ji, Qi, Gui, Fu, Ying, Hao, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Shi was partisan to Tang Situi; others said that Shi, coming from Huaidong, spoke of Zhang Jun's reckless expenditure, and that Jun was dismissed as chief councillor for this. He had nine sons: Gui, Bi, Ji, Qi, Gui, Fu, Ying, Hao, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 子 遵

translations.literal: Son: Zun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zun

sentences.zh: 遵字景嚴，皓仲子也。

translations.literal: Zun's courtesy name was Jingyan; he was Hao's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun, styled Jingyan, was the second son of Hong Hao.

sentences.zh: 自兒時端重如成人，從師業文，不以歲時寒暑輟。

translations.literal: From childhood he was dignified and steady like an adult; he followed teachers in literary studies and did not cease for seasons, cold, or heat.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he carried himself with adult composure. He studied under teachers without breaking off his literary work, summer or winter.

sentences.zh: 父留沙漠，母亡，遵孺慕攀號。

translations.literal: His father remained in the desert; his mother died; Zun in childlike grief wailed and clung.
translations.idiomatic: While his father was detained in the Jin northlands and his mother died, the boy mourned with inconsolable grief.

sentences.zh: 既葬，兄弟即僧舍肄詞業，夜枕不解衣。

translations.literal: After the burial, the brothers at once went to a monastic lodging to pursue examination prose; at night they slept without undressing.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral, he and his brothers moved into a monastery to prepare for the civil examinations, sleeping at night without even taking off their clothes.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭補承務郎，與兄适同試博學宏詞科，中魁選，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed Attendant Gentleman; with his elder brother Shi he jointly sat for the Erudite and Grand Rhetoric examination, ranked first in selection, and was granted jinshi status.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Attendant Gentleman through his father's privilege. He and his elder brother Hong Shi took the Erudite Liturgy examination together, placed first, and received jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 高宗以皓遠使，擢為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Hao was a distant envoy, promoted him to Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hong Hao was still abroad on diplomatic service, Emperor Gaozong appointed Hong Zun Collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，詞科中選即入館，自遵始。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, those selected in the literary examination entered the institutes at once—beginning with Zun.
translations.idiomatic: From the Restoration onward, no one who passed the prestigious literary examination had entered the Hanlin institutes immediately—Hong Zun was the first.

sentences.zh: 宰相秦檜子熺為官長，謦欬為人輕重，遵恬然不附麗。

translations.literal: The chancellor Qin Hui's son Xi was supervising official; a cough or sigh from him determined men's standing, yet Zun remained calm and did not attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui's son Qin Xi was his departmental superior, and his every gesture could make or break a career. Hong Zun remained unperturbed and refused to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 二年弗遷。

translations.literal: Two years passed without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 皓南還，與朝論異，出守。

translations.literal: Hao returned south; he differed from court opinion and was sent out to govern.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Hao returned from the south, his views conflicted with court policy and he was sent out to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 遵遂乞外，通判常、婺、越三州。

translations.literal: Zun then requested an outside appointment and served as vice-prefect of Chang, Wu, and Yue prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun then asked to leave the capital and served as vice-prefect in Changzhou, Wuzhou, and Yuezhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十五年，湯思退薦之，復入為正字。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing, Tang Situi recommended him and he re-entered as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: In 1155 Tang Situi recommended him, and he returned to the capital as Collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八月，兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was additionally appointed acting member of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: That August he was given an additional appointment as acting member of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 湯鵬舉副臺端，密薦為御史。

translations.literal: Tang Pengju was vice censor-in-chief at the Censorate; he secretly recommended Zun for censor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Pengju, a vice censor-in-chief, privately recommended him for a post as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 方賜對而父訃聞。

translations.literal: Just as he was granted an audience, news of his father's death arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to be received in audience when word came of his father's death.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，免喪，召對，極陳父冤，曰：「先臣與龔璹同出疆，璹仕於劉豫，以妄殺兵官為豫所誅，而秦檜贈以節旄，擢用其子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, after mourning ended, he was summoned for audience and fully stated his father's grievance, saying: "My late father went beyond the frontier with Gong Shu; Shu served Liu Yu, was executed by Yu for wantonly killing military officers, yet Qin Hui conferred upon him a staff of command and promoted his son."
translations.idiomatic: In 1158, when his mourning period ended, he was called to audience and pressed his father's case. He said: "My late father and Gong Shu went abroad together on diplomatic service. Shu entered Liu Yu's service and was executed by Yu for unlawfully killing army officers—yet Qin Hui rewarded his family with an imperial command baton and elevated his son."

sentences.zh: 先臣拒金人之命，留十五歲乃得歸，顧南竄嶺外，臣兄弟屏跡在外。

translations.literal: "My late father refused the Jin people's orders, remained fifteen years before he could return, yet was sent fleeing south beyond the mountain passes; we brothers lived hidden outside."
translations.idiomatic: "My father refused to obey the Jin and was detained for fifteen years before he could come home—only to be banished to the far south beyond the passes, while my brothers and I were forced to live in obscurity in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 檜不分忠逆如此。

translations.literal: "Qin Hui thus made no distinction between loyalty and treason."
translations.idiomatic: "This is how Qin Hui failed to distinguish the loyal from the disloyal."

sentences.zh: 」高宗悉為道謗語所起，且曰：「卿再登三館，嘗典書命，今以修注處卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong fully understood it arose from slanderous talk, and also said: "You have twice entered the Three Institutes, once directed book drafts; now I place you in annotation."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong saw that the whole affair had been stirred up by slander, and said: "You have twice risen through the Three Institutes and once held charge of imperial documents. I shall now place you in the annals office."

sentences.zh: 」遂拜起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Imperial Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun was then appointed Imperial Diarist.

sentences.zh: 奏乞以經筵官除罷及封章進對、宴會錫予、講讀問答等事，萃為一書，名之曰《邇英記註》。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that the appointment and dismissal of lecture-hall officials, memorial submissions and audiences, banquets and gifts, lectures and question-and-answer sessions and the like be gathered into one book, named Records of Er'yīng Notes.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned that appointments and dismissals of lecture-hall officials, the presentation of memorials at audience, imperial banquets and gifts, lectures and imperial questions—all these matters be compiled into a single work titled Records of Er'yīng Notes.

sentences.zh: 其後乾道間又有《祥曦殿記註》，實自遵始。

translations.literal: Later in the Qiandao era there was also Notes on the Xiangxi Hall—in truth it began with Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Qiandao reign, Notes on the Xiangxi Hall would follow—the precedent was set by Hong Zun.

sentences.zh: 又因面對，論鑄錢利害，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: Again in a face-to-face audience he discussed the benefits and harms of coin casting; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In another audience he argued the pros and cons of coin minting, and the emperor praised and adopted his views.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎兼權樞密院都承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Bedchamber and concurrently acting Grand Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Bedchamber and concurrently acting chief coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舊制，修注官、經筵官許留身奏事，而近例無有。

translations.literal: Under the old system, annotation officials and lecture-hall officials were permitted to remain after dismissal to present matters, but recent precedent had none.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, annalists and lecture-hall officials were allowed to stay behind after court to memorialize the throne privately, but that practice had fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 遵奏請復舊制，且言起居注未修者十五年，請除見修月進外，每月帶修，皆從之。

translations.literal: Zun memorialized requesting restoration of the old system, and also said the Daily Record had gone unrevised for fifteen years; he requested that apart from the monthly progress now in revision, each month additional revision be carried out—all was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun petitioned to restore the old practice, and noted that the Daily Record had gone unrevised for fifteen years. He asked that, in addition to the monthly progress reports already in place, additional monthly revision work be assigned—all of which was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1159 he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 殿前裨將輔逵轉防禦使，王綱轉團練使，遵言：「近制管軍官十年始一遷，今兩人不滿歲，安得爾？

translations.literal: Adjutant general Fu Kui was transferred to Defender Commandant, Wang Gang to Commander of Militia; Zun said: "Under recent regulations army commanders are promoted once only in ten years; these two men have not completed a year—how can it be so?"
translations.idiomatic: When adjutant Fu Kui was promoted to Defender Commandant and Wang Gang to Militia Commander, Hong Zun protested: "Under current rules army officers receive promotion only once in ten years. These two men have served less than a year—how can this be justified?"

sentences.zh: 」時勳臣子孫多躐居臺省，遵極言乞明有所止。

translations.literal: At the time descendants of meritorious ministers often leaped into posts in the Censorate and secretariat; Zun strongly petitioned requesting clear limits.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many descendants of meritorious officials had leapfrogged into posts in the Censorate and secretariat. Hong Zun forcefully petitioned that clear limits be set.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「正立法，自今功臣子孫序遷至侍從，並令久任在京宮觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Just then establish law—from now on descendants of meritorious officials shall advance in order to attendant posts, and all shall long serve at capital palace chapels."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong replied: "Let us legislate properly: from now on the sons and grandsons of meritorious officials may advance in sequence only as far as attendant-in-waiting ranks, and must serve long terms at palace chapels in the capital."

sentences.zh: 」遵曰：「侍從，朝廷高選，非如磨勘階官，安有遷序之制？

translations.literal: Zun said: "Attendant posts are the court's high selection, not like merit-review step ranks—how can there be a system of sequential promotion?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun replied: "Attendant posts are among the highest appointments in court. They are not like routine merit-review ranks—what sense is there in a ladder of sequential promotion?"

sentences.zh: 」退而上奏言：「今內外將家無慮二十人，若以序遷，不出十年，西清次對皆可坐致。

translations.literal: Retiring, he submitted a memorial saying: "Today military families within and without number nearly twenty; if they advance in sequence, within ten years all posts in the western pure ranks and secondary audiences can be attained by mere sitting."
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, he submitted a memorial: "There are roughly twenty military families in and around the court today. If they advance by seniority alone, within ten years every post in the inner palace secretariat could be filled without effort."

sentences.zh: 太祖開國功臣子孫不過諸司，惟曹彬之子琮、瑋以功名自奮，遂為節度，初不聞有遞遷侍從之例。

translations.literal: Under Taizu, descendants of founding meritorious officials reached no higher than various bureaus; only Cao Bin's sons Cong and Wei by their own merit advanced to become military commissioners; one never heard of examples of successive promotion to attendant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu, the descendants of founding meritors rarely rose above routine bureau posts. Only Cao Bin's sons Cao Cong and Cao Wei, through their own military achievements, became military commissioners—there was never any precedent for hereditary promotion into attendant ranks.

sentences.zh: 今旨一出，使穆清之地類皆將種，非所以示天下。

translations.literal: Once this edict is issued, it will make the pure inner precincts largely military stock—this is not how to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once this edict goes forth, the most exalted inner offices will be filled with military men—a poor message to send the empire.

sentences.zh: 望收還前詔。

translations.literal: I hope the prior edict may be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty withdraw the recent edict.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「瑞昌、興國之間茶商失業，聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: He also said: "Between Ruichang and Xingguo tea merchants lost their livelihood and gathered as bandits."
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "Between Ruichang and Xingguo, tea merchants ruined by unemployment have banded together as robbers."

sentences.zh: 望揭榜開諭，許其自新，願充軍者填刺，願為農者放還。

translations.literal: I hope placards may be posted to enlighten them, permitting reform; those wishing to enlist fill out registers; those wishing to farm be released to return."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that proclamations be posted offering amnesty. Those who wish to enlist should be enrolled; those who wish to return to farming should be released."

sentences.zh: 」上皆可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 論者欲复鄱陽永平、永豐兩監鼓鑄，詔給、舍議，遵曰：「唐有鼓鑄使，國朝或以漕臣兼領，或分道置使，厘為三司。

translations.literal: Advocates wished to restore drum-casting at the Poyang Yongping and Yongfeng mints; an edict ordered drafting and secretariat discussion; Zun said: "The Tang had drum-casting commissioners; our dynasty sometimes had transport officials concurrently in charge, sometimes commissioners by route, divided among three bureaus."
translations.idiomatic: Some officials argued for reopening the Yongping and Yongfeng mints at Poyang. The emperor ordered the draft office and secretariat to deliberate. Hong Zun argued: "The Tang appointed dedicated mint commissioners. In our dynasty responsibility sometimes fell to transport officials, sometimes to route commissioners, and was eventually divided among three bureaus."

sentences.zh: 自中興來，置都大提點，官屬太多，動為州縣之害。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, establishment of grand commissioners had too many subordinates and often harmed prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Restoration, the grand mint commissioners carried too large a staff and frequently became a burden on local government.

sentences.zh: 間者亟行廢罷，又無一定之論，初委運使，又委提刑，又委郡守、貳，號令不一，鼓鑄益少。

translations.literal: Recently repeated abolition had no fixed principle—first entrusted to transport commissioners, then to judicial commissioners, then to prefects and vice-prefects; orders were not unified and drum-casting grew ever fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Recent repeated abolitions have left no consistent policy—authority has shifted from transport commissioners to judicial commissioners to prefects and vice-prefects in turn. With no unified command, mint output has only declined.

sentences.zh: 竊以為復置便。」

translations.literal: I venture to think restoration would be expedient."
translations.idiomatic: I believe reestablishing dedicated mint officers would be the better course."

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，試吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year he served temporarily as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1160 he served temporarily as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 異時選人詣曹改秩，吏倚為市，毫毛不中節，必巧生沮閡，須賂餉滿欲乃止。

translations.literal: Formerly when candidates came to the ministry to change rank, clerks relied on it as a market; the slightest deviation from rules they artfully used to obstruct, requiring bribes to satisfy their desires before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when candidates came to the Ministry of Personnel for rank changes, clerks treated the office as a marketplace. They seized on the smallest irregularity to block proceedings and would not relent until bribes had filled their pockets.

sentences.zh: 遵明與約，苟於大體無害，先行後審，薦員有定限，而舉者周遮重復，或同時一章而巧為兩牘，或當薦五員而輒逾十數，或當舉職官而詭為京狀，或身系常調而妄稱職司，或東西分曹而交錯攙補，或已予复奪而指雲事故，件析枚數，請凡如是者得通劾之。

translations.literal: Zun clearly made a covenant: if no harm to the general principle, advance first and review later; recommended quotas had fixed limits, yet recommenders evaded and duplicated—for example one memorial skillfully split into two documents, or where five should be recommended exceeding ten, or recommending local officials disguised as capital nominations, or persons in regular rotation falsely claiming bureau posts, or east and west offices interleaved to supplement each other, or already granted then reclaimed citing accidents—item by item enumerated, requesting that all such cases be subject to joint impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun laid down clear rules: where no serious principle was at stake, candidates would proceed first and undergo review afterward. Quotas for recommendations were fixed, yet nominators evaded them in every way—splitting one memorial into two documents, recommending ten or more when only five were allowed, presenting local officials as capital appointments, claiming bureau status for men on routine rotation, coordinating nominations across regional offices, or revoking appointments already granted by invoking manufactured pretexts. He listed each abuse in detail and petitioned that all such cases be subject to collective impeachment.

sentences.zh: 舊制，致仕任子，隨所在審敕牒即請行。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for retired officials appointing sons, wherever located they examined the edict and certificate and at once requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, when a retired official's son claimed his hereditary appointment, local authorities could verify the credentials on the spot and issue the appointment immediately.

sentences.zh: 是時，從議者請，必令於元州判奏。

translations.literal: At that time those agreeing with the proposal requested that it must be reported and adjudicated at the original prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the time proponents argued that such cases must be adjudicated in the official's original home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵言：「士大夫或游宦粵、蜀，數千里外，不幸以死。

translations.literal: Zun said: "Scholar-officials sometimes serve in Guang or Shu, thousands of li away, and unhappily die."
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun argued: "Scholar-officials sometimes serve in distant Guangdong or Sichuan, thousands of li from home—and die there."

sentences.zh: 臨終謝事，其家獲歸故里已為至難，今復因此齟齬，反复稽延，是明與惡吏為地也。

translations.literal: At death's end they resign office; for their families to return home is already exceedingly difficult; now again because of this friction, repeated delays—in effect this openly makes ground for wicked clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Even securing permission to retire and bring the body home is already immensely difficult. To add these bureaucratic disputes on top, drawing out delays again and again, is effectively to give corrupt clerks another pretext for extortion."

sentences.zh: 」乃止仍舊貫。

translations.literal: The proposal was halted and the old practice retained.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped and the old practice retained.

sentences.zh: 平江、湖、秀三州水，無以輸秋苗，有司抑令輸麥。

translations.literal: Pingjiang, Hu, and Xiu three prefectures had flooding; unable to deliver autumn grain, supervising officials compelled them to deliver wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang, Huzhou, and Xiuzhou suffered flooding and could not deliver autumn rice tax. Local officials forced them to pay in wheat instead.

sentences.zh: 遵言：「麥價珠不在米下，民困如是，奈何指夏以為秋，衍一以為二，使擠溝壑乎？

translations.literal: Zun said: "Wheat prices are truly not below rice; the people are distressed thus—how can one point to summer as autumn, extending one into two, driving them into gullies and ravines?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun protested: "Wheat is scarcely cheaper than rice. The people are already desperate—how can we treat summer grain as autumn tax, doubling their burden and driving them into ruin?"

sentences.zh: 願量取其半，而被水害者悉免之。

translations.literal: I wish to take half by measure, and those suffering flood harm be wholly exempted."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that half the levy be taken in kind, and that all flood victims be fully exempted."

sentences.zh: 」金人來索絳陽郭小的、安化劉孝恭二百家，遵以蜀之李特可為至戒，願以根集未足為解，淹引日月報之。

translations.literal: The Jin people came to demand two hundred households of Guo Xiaodi of Jiangyang and Liu Xiaogong of Anhua; Zun took Shu's Li Te as the utmost warning, wished to use incomplete compilation of records as explanation, and delayed month upon month in reporting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin demanded two hundred households—the families of Guo Xiaodi of Jiangyang and Liu Xiaogong of Anhua—Hong Zun cited Li Te's rebellion in Shu as a cautionary warning. He pleaded that record-gathering was incomplete and deliberately stalled for months in his replies.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician and concurrently Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 汪澈論湯思退罷相，遵行製無貶詞，澈以為言。

translations.literal: Wang Che memorialized on Tang Situi's dismissal as chancellor; Zun drafted the edict without censorious language; Che spoke against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Che attacked Tang Situi's dismissal from the chancellorship, Hong Zun drafted the imperial rescript without a word of censure—drawing Wang Che's criticism.

sentences.zh: 遂丐去，以徽猷閣直學士提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He then requested to leave, and was appointed as Attendant Gentleman of the Huayou Pavilion to direct Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to resign and was given the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Huayou Pavilion, charged with overseeing Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，金主完顏亮命其尚書蘇保衡由海道窺二浙，朝廷以浙西副總管李寶御之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the Jin ruler Wanyan Liang ordered his Minister Su Baoheng to probe the Two Zhes by sea route; the court had Western Zhe Deputy Commander Li Bao resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1161 the Jin emperor Wanyan Liang sent his minister Su Baoheng by sea to reconnoiter the Zhejiang coast. The court assigned Li Bao, deputy commander of Western Zhe, to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 寶駐兵平江，守臣朱翌素與寶異，朝議以遵嘗薦寶，乃命遵知平江。

translations.literal: Bao stationed troops at Pingjiang; the guarding official Zhu Yi had long differed with Bao; court discussion because Zun had once recommended Bao then ordered Zun to govern Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao was encamped at Pingjiang, but the prefect Zhu Yi had long been at odds with him. Because Hong Zun had once recommended Li Bao, the court appointed Hong Zun prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 及寶以舟師搗膠西，凡資糧、器械、舟楫皆遵供億，寶成功而歸，遵之助為多。

translations.literal: When Bao with naval forces struck Jiaoxi, all provisions, weapons, and vessels were supplied by Zun; Bao succeeded and returned—Zun's assistance was great.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bao struck the Jin fleet at Jiaoxi, Hong Zun furnished all provisions, weapons, and ships. Li Bao's victory owed much to his support.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸金陵，禁衛士丐索無藝，它郡隨與不厭。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Jinling, palace guards begged and demanded without restraint; other prefectures gave whenever asked without satiation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jinling, his guard troops made boundless demands for supplies. Other prefectures met every request without limit.

sentences.zh: 至吳，乃相告曰：「內翰在此，汝毋复然。

translations.literal: Reaching Wu, they told one another: "The Academician-in-waiting is here—you must not again be so."
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Wu, word spread among the troops: "The Hanlin Academician is here—don't try that again."

sentences.zh: 」先是，朝廷慮商舶為賊得，悉拘入官，既而不返，並海縣團萃巨艦及募水手、民兵，皆縶留未得去。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court fearing merchant ships would fall to bandits had all impounded for the state; afterward not returned; coastal counties gathered great ships and recruited sailors and militia—all detained unable to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court, fearing merchant vessels might fall into enemy hands, had impounded them for state use—but never returned them. Coastal counties had also gathered large ships and conscripted sailors and militia, all of whom remained detained and unable to leave.

sentences.zh: 遵因對論之，以船還商，而聽水手自便，吳人德之。

translations.literal: Zun used an audience to discuss it, returning ships to merchants and permitting sailors their own convenience; the people of Wu were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun raised the matter at audience, restored the ships to merchants, and freed the sailors to go as they pleased. The people of Wu were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 知隆興元年貢舉，拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He directed the Longxing first year examination and was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the civil examinations of 1163 and was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 壽康殿產金芝十二，同列議表賀，遵引李文靖奏災異故事風止之。

translations.literal: Twelve golden fungi grew in the Shoukang Hall; colleagues discussed a congratulatory memorial; Zun cited Attendant Gentleman Li's memorial on prodigies and calamities as precedent and stopped it by persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: When twelve golden lingzhi mushrooms appeared in the Shoukang Hall, his colleagues proposed a congratulatory memorial. Hong Zun cited the precedent of Li Wenjing's memorial treating such portents as omens and dissuaded them.

sentences.zh: 薦眉山李燾、永嘉鄭伯熊及林光朝，未及用，會湯思退為左相，而次相張浚罷，御史周璪策遵且超遷，上章致劾，上亟徙置他官。

translations.literal: He recommended Meishan's Li Tao, Yongjia's Zheng Boxiong, and Lin Guangchao; before they could be used, Tang Situi became Left Chancellor while Second Chancellor Zhang Jun was dismissed; Censor Zhou Cang plotted that Zun would soon leap in promotion, submitted impeachment; the emperor hastily transferred and placed him in another office.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Li Tao of Meishan, Zheng Boxiong of Yongjia, and Lin Guangchao—but before they could be appointed, Tang Situi became chief councillor and vice-councillor Zhang Jun was dismissed. Censor Zhou Cang, anticipating that Hong Zun would leap ahead in rank, submitted an impeachment. The emperor quickly moved Hong Zun to another post.

sentences.zh: 遵不能安位，連章乞免，訖與御史俱去。

translations.literal: Zun could not rest in his post, submitted successive memorials requesting dismissal, ending with both himself and the censor departing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun could not remain in office and submitted repeated requests for dismissal. In the end both he and the censor left their posts.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，以端明殿學士提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Duanming Hall to direct Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That July he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Duanming Hall and assigned to oversee Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，起知信州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao he was recalled to govern Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1170 he was recalled to serve as prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙知太平州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiping Prefecture as prefect.

sentences.zh: 前守周璪以嘗論遵，聞遵來，不俟合符馳去。

translations.literal: The former prefect Zhou Cang because he had once impeached Zun, upon hearing Zun was coming, did not wait for the transfer tally and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: The outgoing prefect Zhou Cang—who had once impeached Hong Zun—fled before the formal transfer of authority could even take place, upon hearing of Hong Zun's appointment.

sentences.zh: 遵追餞至十里，勞苦如平時，曰：「君當官而行，我何怨？

translations.literal: Zun pursued to send him off ten li, treating him with courtesy as in normal times, saying: "You acted as an official should—I bear what resentment?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun rode ten li to see him off and treated him with the same courtesy as always, saying: "You were only doing your duty as an official—why should I resent you?"

sentences.zh: 」聞者以為盛德。

translations.literal: Hearers considered it great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 圩田壞，民失業，遵鳩民築圩凡萬數。

translations.literal: Polder fields were ruined; the people lost livelihood; Zun mobilized the people to build polders totaling tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When flood walls collapsed and farmers lost their livelihoods, Hong Zun organized the people to rebuild polders by the ten thousands.

sentences.zh: 方冬盛寒，遵躬履其間，載酒食親餉饁，恩意傾盡，人忘其勞。

translations.literal: Just in winter's bitter cold, Zun personally walked among them, carrying wine and food to personally supply meals; his kindness poured fully forth; people forgot their labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the depth of winter he walked the worksites himself, bringing wine and food to feed the laborers with his own hands. His care was so wholehearted that the people scarcely felt their exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 運使張松忌功，妄奏圩未嘗決，民未嘗轉徙，必責圩戶自閼築，且裁省募工錢米之半。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhang Song envied his achievement, falsely memorialized the polders had never broken, the people never relocated, insisted polder households rebuild at their own expense, and cut recruited labor funds and grain by half.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Zhang Song, jealous of his achievement, falsely reported that no polder had breached and no farmers had been displaced. He insisted polder households repair the works themselves and cut the allocated labor funds and grain by half.

sentences.zh: 遵連疏爭，至乞遣朝臣覆按。

translations.literal: Zun submitted successive memorials disputing, even requesting dispatch of court officials to reinvestigate.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun submitted memorial after memorial in protest, going so far as to request a court investigation.

sentences.zh: 於是將作少監馬希言、監察御史陳舉善狎至，黜松言，圩遂成，合四百五十有五。

translations.literal: Thereupon Assistant Director of Palace Buildings Ma Xiyan and Supervising Censor Chen Jushan arrived in succession, rejected Song's claims, and the polders were completed—455 in all.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of Palace Buildings Ma Xiyan and Supervising Censor Chen Jushan were dispatched in turn. They rejected Zhang Song's account, and the polders were completed—a total of 455.

sentences.zh: 松無所洩其忿，則別治溧水永豐圩，來調丁、米、木，數甚廣。

translations.literal: Song having no outlet for his anger then separately undertook the Lishui Yongfeng polder, coming to requisition laborers, grain, and timber in very broad numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to vent his resentment elsewhere, Zhang Song turned to building the Yongfeng polder in Lishui County, requisitioning labor, grain, and timber on a vast scale from Hong Zun's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「郡當歲儉，方振卹流移，勸分乞糴，如自刲其股以充喉，不暇食，況能飽他人腹哉。

translations.literal: Zun said: "The prefecture faces famine this year; we are just relieving displaced persons, encouraging sharing and begging grain purchases—as if cutting one's own thigh to fill the throat, with no leisure to eat—how much less can one fill another's belly?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun replied: "The prefecture is in the grip of famine. We are already providing relief to refugees and begging grain wherever we can. To meet these demands would be like cutting flesh from our own leg to feed our mouth when we are starving—how can we fill another man's belly?"

sentences.zh: 」執不從。

translations.literal: He firmly refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 楚地旱，旁縣振贍者慮不早，施置失後先，或得米而亡以炊，或闔戶莩藉而廩不至。

translations.literal: The Chu region had drought; neighboring counties giving relief feared being too late; arrangements lost proper sequence—some received grain but had nothing to cook with, some whole households lay starving while granaries did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: A drought struck the region. Neighboring counties that tried to provide relief acted too late or in the wrong order. Some families received grain but had no fuel to cook it; others starved at home while grain sat undelivered in the warehouses.

sentences.zh: 遵簡賓佐，隨遠近壯老以差賦給，蠲租至十九，又告糴於江西，得活者不啻萬計。

translations.literal: Zun selected aides, according to distance and age of strong and old differentiated distribution; rent remitted up to nine parts in ten, also purchased grain in Jiangxi—the number saved was no less than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zun delegated his staff to distribute relief by distance and by the needs of the young and old. He remitted up to ninety percent of land tax and purchased grain from Jiangxi. Tens of thousands of lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 戍兵乘時盜利，曹伍剽於野，盡執拘以歸其軍。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers seized the moment to steal for profit; squads plundered in the wilds—all were seized and detained and returned to their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops took advantage of the crisis to loot the countryside. Hong Zun arrested every band and returned the men to their units.

sentences.zh: 故當大札瘥而邑落晏然。

translations.literal: Therefore when great plague passed, villages and hamlets were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when plague struck the region, the towns and villages remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 徙知建​​康府、江東安撫使兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Jiankang Prefecture, Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner concurrently Mobile Palatial Residence Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Nanjing as prefect, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, and caretaker of the imperial traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 孝宗諭當制舍人范成大，褒其治績，且許入覲。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong instructed Drafter Fan Chengda to praise his governing achievements and moreover permit him audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong instructed Fan Chengda, who held drafting duty, to compose an edict praising Hong Zun's administrative record and granting him permission to appear at court.

sentences.zh: 子 邁

translations.literal: Son: Mai
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong Mai

sentences.zh: 邁字景盧，皓季子也。

translations.literal: Mai's courtesy name was Jinglu; he was Hao's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai, styled Jinglu, was the youngest son of Hong Hao.

sentences.zh: 幼讀書日數千言，一過目輒不忘，博極載籍，雖稗官虞初，釋老傍行，靡不涉獵。

translations.literal: From youth in reading he covered thousands of words daily; once seen he never forgot; he exhaustively mastered canonical texts—even unofficial histories, Yu Chu tales, Buddhist and Daoist side texts, none he did not browse.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he read thousands of characters daily and never forgot what he had seen once. He mastered the classics so thoroughly that he ranged even through folk tales, collections like Yu Chu, and Buddhist and Daoist writings—nothing was outside his reading.

sentences.zh: 從二兄試博學宏詞科，邁獨被黜。

translations.literal: Following his two elder brothers he sat for the Erudite and Grand Rhetoric examination; Mai alone was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Erudite Liturgy examination alongside his two elder brothers—but only Hong Mai failed.

sentences.zh: 紹興十五年始中第，授兩浙轉運司幹辦公事，入為敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing he placed in the examination and was appointed staff officer of the Two-Zhe Transport Commission; he entered as revision officer of the Statutes Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1145 he passed the examination and was appointed staff officer of the Two-Zhe Transport Commission, then became a reviser in the Statutes Office.

sentences.zh: 皓忤秦檜投閒，檜憾未已，御史汪勃論邁知其父不靖之謀，遂出添差教授福州。

translations.literal: Hao offended Qin Hui and was cast aside; Hui's resentment had not ceased; Censor Wang Bo memorialized that Mai knew his father's unruly designs, and he was sent out as supernumerary professor at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Hao clashed with Qin Hui and was sidelined, Qin's resentment did not end. Censor Wang Bo charged that Hong Mai had known of his father's "disloyal" intentions, and Hong Mai was transferred out as supernumerary professor at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部郎兼禮部。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Department Director of Personnel concurrently of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become department director of the Ministries of Personnel and Rites.

sentences.zh: 上居顯仁皇后喪，當孟饗，禮官未知所從，邁請遣宰相分祭，奏可。

translations.literal: The emperor was in mourning for Empress Dowager Xianren; when the first-month sacrifice came, ritual officials did not know which course to follow; Mai requested dispatching chancellors to divide sacrifices—the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was in mourning for Empress Dowager Xianren, ritual officials were uncertain how to conduct the first seasonal sacrifice. Hong Mai proposed that the chancellors perform the rites separately—and the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 除樞密檢詳文字。

translations.literal: He was appointed Text Examiner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed textual reviewer in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建議令民入粟贖罪，以紓國用，又請嚴法駕出入之儀。

translations.literal: He proposed allowing the people to submit grain to redeem crimes, to ease state expenditure; he also requested strict regulation of the imperial carriage's egress and ingress ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed allowing citizens to redeem offenses with grain contributions to ease state finances, and also called for stricter protocol for the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，議欽宗諡，邁曰：「淵聖北狩不返，臣民悲痛，當如楚人立懷王之義，號懷宗，以系復仇之意。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Emperor Qinzong's posthumous title was discussed, Mai said: "The Deep and Sagely Emperor went north on hunt and did not return; officials and people grieve; one should follow the meaning of the Chu people establishing King Huai, title him Emperor Huaizong, to maintain the intent of revenge."
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, when the court debated Emperor Qinzong's posthumous title, Hong Mai argued: "The Captive Emperor never returned from the north. The grief of the court and people is unabated. We should follow the precedent of the Chu establishing King Huai of Chu and style him Emperor Huaizong, to keep alive the resolve for national restoration."

sentences.zh: 」不用。

translations.literal: It was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 吳璘病篤，朝論欲徙吳拱代之。

translations.literal: Wu Lin was gravely ill; court opinion wanted to transfer Wu Gong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Lin fell gravely ill, court opinion favored transferring Wu Gong to replace him.

sentences.zh: 邁曰：「吳氏以功握蜀兵三十年，宜有以新民觀聽，毋使尾大不掉。

translations.literal: Mai said: "The Wu clan, on merit, has held Shu troops for thirty years—there should be something to renew the people's perception, lest the tail grow too large to wag.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai argued: "The Wu family has commanded Sichuan's armies on merit for thirty years. The court should give the people some sign of renewal and not let the branch grow so powerful that it cannot be controlled.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事葉義問出視師，奏以邁參議軍事，至鎮江，聞瓜洲官軍與金人相持，遑遽失措。

translations.literal: Commissioner-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs Ye Yiwen went out to inspect the army, memorialized to have Mai participate in military deliberations; arriving at Zhenjiang, hearing government troops at Guazhou locked in stalemate with the Jurchens, he was flustered and lost composure.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yiwen, commissioner-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, went out to inspect the troops and had Hong Mai appointed to advise on military affairs. When they reached Zhenjiang and learned that government forces at Guazhou were deadlocked with the Jurchens, Ye panicked and lost his composure.

sentences.zh: 會建康走驛告急，義問遽欲還，邁力止之曰：「今退師，無益京口勝敗之數，而金陵聞返旆，人心動搖，不可。

translations.literal: Just then a courier from Jiankang arrived in alarm; Yiwen suddenly wanted to return; Mai forcefully stopped him, saying: "To withdraw the army now would not help the tally of victory or defeat at Jingkou, and if Jinling hears of returning banners, popular sentiment will waver—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When an urgent courier arrived from Jiankang, Ye Yiwen wanted to pull back at once. Hong Mai forcefully dissuaded him: "A withdrawal now would not change the outcome at Jingkou, and if Nanjing hears that our banners are turning back, morale will collapse. That must not be done.

sentences.zh: 」遷左司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三十二年春，金主褒遣左監軍高忠建來告登位，且議和，邁為接伴使，知閣門張掄副之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-second year, the Jin ruler Bao sent Left Army Supervisor Gao Zhongjian to announce his accession and also discuss peace; Mai served as reception commissioner, with Palace Gate Commissioner Zhang Lun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1162, the Jin emperor Bao sent Left Army Supervisor Gao Zhongjian to announce his accession and discuss peace. Hong Mai served as reception commissioner, with Palace Gate Commissioner Zhang Lun as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 上謂執政曰：「向日講和，本為梓宮、太后，雖屈己卑辭，有所不憚。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "When we negotiated peace before, it was fundamentally for the imperial coffin and the empress dowager—though humbling oneself with deferential language, there was nothing I shrank from.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers: "When we negotiated peace before, it was above all for the imperial coffin and the empress dowager. I was willing to humble myself and use deferential language for that.

sentences.zh: 今兩國之盟已絕，名稱以何為正，疆土以何為準，朝見之儀，歲幣之數，所宜先定。

translations.literal: Now the alliance between the two states is severed—what titles should be used, what borders should serve as standard, the ceremonies of court audience, the amount of annual tribute—all these should first be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the alliance between the two states is broken, we must first settle what titles are proper, what borders should serve as the standard, the ceremonies of court audience, and the amount of annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 」及邁、掄入辭，上又曰：「朕料此事終歸於和，欲首議名分，而土地次之。

translations.literal: When Mai and Lun came for farewell audience, the emperor again said: "I judge this matter will ultimately end in peace; I wish first to negotiate status and titles, with territory second.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Mai and Zhang Lun came to take leave, the emperor added: "I expect this matter will end in peace after all. I want status and titles settled first, and territory second.

sentences.zh: 」邁於是奏更接伴禮數，凡十有四事。

translations.literal: Mai thereupon memorialized to revise the reception protocol—fourteen items in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai then memorialized to revise the reception protocol in fourteen points.

sentences.zh: 自渡江以來，屈己含忍多過禮，至是一切殺之，用敵國體，凡遠迎及引接金銀等皆罷。

translations.literal: Since crossing the Yangzi, self-abasement and forbearance had exceeded proper ritual many times—at this point everything was cut back, using equal-state protocol; all distant greeting and escort with gold and silver were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court had crossed the Yangzi, it had humbled itself and endured humiliations that far exceeded proper ritual. Hong Mai now cut all of that back and insisted on equal-state protocol. Distant greeting ceremonies and the presentation of gold and silver on escort were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 既而高忠建有責臣禮及取新復州郡之議，邁以聞，且奏言：「土疆實利不可與，禮際虛名不足惜。

translations.literal: Soon after, Gao Zhongjian raised the topics of ministerial deference and reclaiming newly recovered prefectures and districts; Mai reported this and also memorialized: "Territorial gains of real benefit cannot be ceded; ceremonial titles are empty names not worth sparing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongjian raised demands for ministerial deference and the return of newly recovered prefectures and districts, Hong Mai reported this to the throne and argued: "Territory of real strategic value must not be surrendered; ceremonial titles are empty names not worth clinging to.

sentences.zh: 」禮部侍郎黃中聞之，亟奏曰：「名定實隨，百世不易，不可謂虛。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Huang Zhong heard of this and urgently memorialized: "When the name is fixed, reality follows—unchanged for a hundred generations; it cannot be called empty.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Huang Zhong heard of this and urgently memorialized: "When the name is fixed, reality follows, and that does not change for a hundred generations. Titles cannot be called empty.

sentences.zh: 土疆得失，一彼一此，不可謂實。

translations.literal: Gain and loss of territory shifts between them—it cannot be called real.
translations.idiomatic: Territorial gains and losses shift back and forth between the two states. That cannot be called a matter of solid advantage.

sentences.zh: 」兵部侍郎陳俊卿亦謂：「先正名分，名分正則國威張，而歲幣亦可損矣。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Chen Junqing also said: "First fix status and titles; when status is correct, national prestige expands, and annual tribute can also be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Chen Junqing also argued: "Fix status and titles first. Once they are correct, national prestige will rise and annual tribute can be reduced as well."

sentences.zh: 進起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to diarist of the palace.

sentences.zh: 時議遣使報金國聘，三月丁巳，詔侍從、臺諫各舉可備使命者一人。
