translations.literal: At the time it was debated to dispatch envoys to return the Jin state's visit; on dingsi day of the third month, an edict ordered attendants and remonstrance officials each to recommend one person fit for diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated sending envoys to return the Jin visit. On the dingsi day of the third month, an edict ordered palace attendants and remonstrance officials each to recommend one man fit for diplomatic service.

sentences.zh: 初，邁之接伴也，既持舊禮折伏金使，至是，慨然請行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mai served as reception commissioner, he had already enforced the old protocol to subdue the Jin envoy; at this point he resolutely volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Mai had served as reception commissioner, he had already used the revised protocol to force the Jin envoy into submission. Now he volunteered resolutely to go himself.

sentences.zh: 於是假翰林學士，充賀登位使，欲令金稱兄弟敵國而歸河南地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was temporarily granted Hanlin Academician and appointed envoy to congratulate the accession, intending to have the Jin call them brother equal states and return the Henan territory.
translations.idiomatic: He was then temporarily granted the title of Hanlin academician and appointed envoy to congratulate the new Jin ruler, with the aim of securing equal-state status as brother kingdoms and the return of Henan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊子，邁辭行，書用敵國禮，高宗親札賜邁等曰：「祖宗陵寢，隔闊三十年，不得以時灑掃祭祀，心實痛之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, summer, on wuzi day, Mai took leave to depart; the letter used equal-state protocol; Emperor Gaozong personally wrote to Mai and the others: "The tombs of our ancestors—separated for thirty years, unable to be swept and sacrificed to in season—the heart truly grieves.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the fourth month, Hong Mai took leave to depart. His credentials used equal-state protocol. Emperor Gaozong wrote to Hong Mai and his party in his own hand: "Our ancestral tombs have lain beyond reach for thirty years, and we have been unable to sweep and sacrifice to them in their season. That pain is real.

sentences.zh: 若彼能以河南地見歸，必欲居尊如故，正复屈己，亦何所惜。

translations.literal: If they can return the Henan territory, even if they insist on keeping their superior position as before, to humble oneself again—what is there to regret?
translations.idiomatic: If they will return Henan, I am willing to humble myself again and let them keep their superior position as before. What would there be to regret?

sentences.zh: 」邁奏言：「山東之兵未解，則兩國之好不成。

translations.literal: Mai memorialized: "If the armies in Shandong are not disbanded, then good relations between the two states cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai memorialized: "If the armies in Shandong are not withdrawn, a lasting peace between the two states cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: 」至燕，金閣門見國書，呼曰：「不如式。

translations.literal: Arriving at Yan, the Jin Gate Office saw the state letter and cried out: "It does not match the format.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yan, the Jin Gate Office inspected the state letter and shouted: "This does not conform to the required form.

sentences.zh: 」抑令使人於表中改陪臣二字，朝見之儀必欲用舊禮。

translations.literal: They forced the envoys to change the two characters "subordinate minister" in the memorial table; the audience ceremony they insisted on using the old protocol.
translations.idiomatic: They forced the envoys to change the words "subordinate minister" in the memorial of credence and insisted that the audience ceremony follow the old protocol.

sentences.zh: 邁初執不可，既而金鎖使館，自旦及暮水漿不通，三日乃得見。

translations.literal: Mai at first held firm that it could not be done; soon after the Jin locked the envoy lodge—from dawn to dusk no water or food passed through; only after three days did they obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai at first refused. The Jin then locked the envoy lodge and cut off food and drink from dawn to dusk. Only after three days were the envoys granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 金人語極不遜，大都督懷忠議欲質留，左丞相張浩持不可，乃遣還。

translations.literal: The Jurchen speech was extremely insolent; Grand Commissioner Huai Zhong proposed detaining them as hostages; Left Chancellor Zhang Hao argued it could not be done, and they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens spoke with extreme insolence. Grand Commissioner Huai Zhong proposed detaining the envoys as hostages, but Left Chancellor Zhang Hao objected, and the party was sent back.

sentences.zh: 七月，邁回朝，則孝宗已即位矣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Mai returned to court—and Emperor Xiaozong had already ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hong Mai returned to court, by which time Emperor Xiaozong had already ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史張震以邁使金辱命，論罷之。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Zhang Zhen, on the grounds that Mai's mission to the Jin had disgraced his commission, memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Censor Zhang Zhen memorialized for Hong Mai's dismissal on the grounds that his mission to the Jin had disgraced the imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 明年，起知泉州。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled to govern Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，复知吉州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, he was again appointed to govern Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 he was again appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 入對，遂除起居舍人，直前言：「起居注皆據諸處關報，始加修纂，雖有日曆、時政記，亦莫得書。

translations.literal: Upon audience at court, he was appointed Diarist and spoke forthrightly: "The Daily Records rely on reports from various offices before revision—even with the Calendar and Records of Current Policy, nothing can be written.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared at court, he was appointed diarist and spoke plainly: "The Daily Records depend on reports from various offices and are only then compiled. Even with the Calendar and Records of Current Policy, little of real substance gets written down.

sentences.zh: 景祐故事，有《邇英延義二閣註記》，凡經筵侍臣出處、封章進對、宴會賜予，皆用存記。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou precedent there was the Record of the Eying and Yanyi Halls—all lecturing officials' comings and goings, memorial submissions and audience responses, banquets and bestowals were all recorded for preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingyou precedent there was the Record of the Eying and Yanyi Halls, in which the attendance of lecture officials, memorial submissions and imperial responses, banquets, and bestowals were all preserved.

sentences.zh: 十年間稍廢不續，陛下言動皆罔聞知，恐非命侍本意。

translations.literal: Over ten years it was gradually abandoned and not continued—Your Majesty's words and actions are all unknown; I fear this is not the original intent of appointing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Over the past decade that practice has largely lapsed. Your Majesty's words and actions go unrecorded, which I fear was not the purpose of appointing palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 乞令講讀官自今各以日得聖語關送修注官，令講筵所牒報，使謹錄之，因今所御殿名曰《祥曦記註》。

translations.literal: I beg that lecturing officials from now on each day transmit the sage utterances received to the revising diarists, with the lecture hall issuing reports for careful recording, naming it after the hall now used: Record of Xiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that lecturing officials hereafter transmit each day's imperial utterances to the revising diarists, with the lecture hall issuing regular reports so that they may be carefully recorded, and that the record be named the Xiangxi Annals after the hall now in use.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷起居郎，拜中書舍人兼侍讀、直學士院，仍參史事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Palace Diarist, appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat concurrently Lecturer and Academician of the Hanlin Institute, still participating in historical compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to palace diarist and appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, concurrently lecturer and academician of the Hanlin Institute, while continuing to participate in historical compilation.

sentences.zh: 父忠宣、兄适、遵皆歷此三職，邁又踵之。

translations.literal: His father Zhongxuan, elder brothers Shi and Zun had all held these three posts; Mai followed in their footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: His father, posthumously titled Zhongxuan, and his elder brothers Hong Shi and Hong Zun had all held these three posts; Hong Mai now followed in their footsteps.

sentences.zh: 邁奏：「三省事無鉅細，必先經中書書黃，宰執書押，當制舍人書行，然後過門下，給事中書讀，如給、舍有所建明，則封黃具奏，以聽上旨。

translations.literal: Mai memorialized: "Affairs of the Three Departments, none great or small, must first pass through the Secretariat's yellow draft; chancellors sign and approve; the drafting vice minister writes for promulgation; then it passes the Gate Department, where the supervisory recipient reads it; if recipient or drafter has proposals, they seal the yellow draft and memorialize together, awaiting the imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai memorialized: "No matter how great or small, affairs of the Three Departments must first be drafted in yellow at the Secretariat, signed by the chancellors, and written for promulgation by the drafting vice minister. Only then do they pass to the Gate Department for review by the supervisory recipient. If the recipient or drafter has proposals, they seal the yellow draft and memorialize together for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 惟樞密院既得旨，即書黃過門下，例不送中書，謂之『密白』，則封駁之職似有所偏，況今宰相兼樞密，因而厘正，不為有嫌。

translations.literal: Only the Bureau of Military Affairs, once obtaining the decree, immediately drafts in yellow and passes the Gate Department—by precedent not sent to the Secretariat, called 'secret white'—then the remonstrance and rejection function seems somewhat partial; moreover now chancellors concurrently hold the Bureau of Military Affairs—therefore rectifying this would not involve impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Bureau of Military Affairs, once it receives the imperial decision, drafts in yellow and sends the document directly to the Gate Department without passing the Secretariat—a practice called 'secret white.' That leaves the review and remonstrance function incomplete. Now that chancellors also head the Bureau of Military Affairs, correcting this would involve no impropriety.

sentences.zh: 望詔樞密院。

translations.literal: I hope the Bureau of Military Affairs may be edicted.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Bureau of Military Affairs be so instructed.

sentences.zh: 凡已被制敕，並關左右省依三省書黃，以示重出命之意。

translations.literal: All already issued edicts should also notify the Left and Right Departments according to the Three Departments' yellow draft practice, to show the weight of issuing orders.
translations.idiomatic: All promulgated edicts should also be reported to the Left and Right Departments according to the Three Departments' yellow-draft procedure, to show the weight of imperial command.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，除知贛州，起學宮，造浮梁，士民安之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to govern Ganzhou, built a school palace, constructed a floating bridge—scholars and people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed prefect of Ganzhou. He built a school and a floating bridge, and scholars and common people alike were put at ease.

sentences.zh: 郡兵素驕，小不如欲則跋扈，郡歲遣千人戍九江，是歲，或怵以至則留不復返，眾遂反戈。

translations.literal: Prefecture troops were by nature arrogant; if slightly dissatisfied they became overbearing; the prefecture each year sent a thousand men to garrison Jiujiang; that year some were incited that once arrived they would be kept and not return—the crowd then turned their weapons around.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural troops were habitually unruly and became overbearing whenever their wishes were even slightly thwarted. Each year the prefecture sent a thousand men to garrison Jiujiang. That year some were incited to believe that once they arrived they would be kept there and never allowed home, and the men turned on their officers.

sentences.zh: 民訛言相驚，百姓恟懼。

translations.literal: Among the people false rumors alarmed one another; the common people were panicked.
translations.idiomatic: False rumors spread among the people, and the populace was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 邁不為動，但遣一校婉說之，俾歸營，眾皆聽，垂橐而入，徐詰什五長兩人，械送潯陽，斬於市。

translations.literal: Mai was unmoved, only sending one officer to persuade them gently, causing them to return to camp—all obeyed; carrying their bags they entered; slowly he interrogated two squad leaders of ten and five, sent them under restraint to Xunyang, and executed them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai remained calm. He sent one officer to reason with the men and persuade them back to camp, and they obeyed. When they entered carrying their packs, he quietly identified two squad leaders and had them bound and sent to Xunyang, where they were executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 辛卯歲饑，贛適中熟，邁移粟濟鄰郡。

translations.literal: In the xinmao year there was famine; Gan had just reached a moderate harvest; Mai transferred grain to aid neighboring prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In a xinmao year of famine, Ganzhou had just enjoyed a moderate harvest, and Hong Mai transferred grain to relieve neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 僚屬有諫止者，邁笑曰：「秦、越瘠肥，臣子義耶？

translations.literal: Staff members admonished him to stop; Mai laughed and said: "When Qin is lean and Yue is fat—is that a minister's duty?
translations.idiomatic: When staff members urged him to stop, Hong Mai laughed and said: "Are we ministers only when Qin is starving and Yue is fat?

sentences.zh: 」尋知建寧府。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed to govern Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 富民有睚眥殺人衷刃篡獄者，久拒捕，邁正其罪，黥流嶺外。

translations.literal: A wealthy man who had killed over a petty grudge, concealed a blade, and seized the prison had long refused capture; Mai judged his crime, tattooed and exiled him beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man who had killed over a petty grudge, concealed a blade on his person, and seized control of the jail had long evaded capture. Hong Mai tried him, had him tattooed, and exiled him beyond the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 十一年[1]，知婺州，奏：「金華田多沙，勢不受水，五日不雨則旱，故境內陂湖最當繕治。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, governing Wuzhou, he memorialized: "Jinhua fields are mostly sandy; the terrain does not hold water—five days without rain brings drought; therefore ponds and lakes within the territory most need repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, as prefect of Wuzhou, he memorialized: "The fields of Jinhua are mostly sandy and hold little water. Five days without rain bring drought, so the ponds and lakes within the prefecture most urgently need repair.

sentences.zh: 命耕者出力，田主出穀，凡為公私塘堰及湖，總之為八百三十七所。

translations.literal: He ordered cultivators to supply labor, landowners to supply grain; all public and private ponds, weirs, and lakes totaled 837 projects.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered cultivators to supply labor and landowners to supply grain. Public and private ponds, weirs, and lakes repaired in all numbered 837.

sentences.zh: 」婺軍素無律，春給衣，欲以緡易帛，吏不可，則群呼嘯聚於郡將之治，郡將惴恐，姑息如其欲。

translations.literal: Wuzhou troops by nature had no discipline; in spring when clothing was issued, they wanted to exchange cash strings for silk cloth; the officials refused, then they gathered in a clamoring mob at the military commissioner's office; the commissioner was fearful and indulgent, giving them what they wanted.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuzhou garrison had long lacked discipline. Each spring when clothing was issued, the soldiers wanted to exchange cash for silk cloth. When officials refused, they gathered in a shouting mob at the military commissioner's office. The commissioner, fearful, indulged them.

sentences.zh: 邁至，眾狃前事，至以飛語榜譙門。

translations.literal: When Mai arrived, the crowd was accustomed to prior affairs, going so far as to post slanderous placards at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Mai arrived, the men, emboldened by past indulgence, went so far as to post slanderous placards at the gate.

sentences.zh: 邁以計逮捕四十有八人，置之理，黨眾相嗾，哄擁邁轎，邁曰：「彼罪人也，汝等何預？

translations.literal: Mai by stratagem arrested forty-eight persons and put them on trial; the faction incited one another and crowded around Mai's sedan chair in a hubbub; Mai said: "They are criminals—what concern is it of yours?
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai by stratagem arrested forty-eight men and put them on trial. The faction incited one another and crowded around his sedan chair in uproar. Hong Mai said: "They are criminals. What business is that of yours?

sentences.zh: 」眾逡巡散去。

translations.literal: The crowd hesitated and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd hesitated and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 邁戮首惡二人，梟之市，餘黥撻有差，莫敢嘩者。

translations.literal: Mai executed the two ringleaders and displayed their heads in the market; the rest received tattooing and flogging in varying degrees—none dared make an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai executed the two ringleaders and displayed their heads in the market. The rest received tattooing and flogging in varying degrees, and none dared raise an outcry again.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上語輔臣曰：「不謂書生能臨事達權。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor told chief ministers: "I did not expect a scholar could handle affairs with timely discretion.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the emperor told his chief ministers: "I did not expect a scholar to handle a crisis with such timely discretion.

sentences.zh: 」特遷敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Gentleman of Attendant at the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to gentleman attendant at the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明年，召對，首論淮東邊備六要地：曰海陵，曰喻洳，曰鹽城，曰寶應，曰清口，曰盱眙。

translations.literal: The next year summoned for audience, he first discussed six key points of Huaidong frontier defense: called Hailing, called Yuru, called Yancheng, called Baoying, called Qingkou, called Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, summoned for audience, he first discussed six key points of Huaidong frontier defense: Hailing, Yuru, Yancheng, Baoying, Qingkou, and Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 謂宜修城池，嚴屯兵，立遊樁，益戍卒。

translations.literal: He said walls and moats should be repaired, garrison troops strictly deployed, patrol piles established, and frontier soldiers augmented.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that city walls should be repaired, garrisons tightened, patrol stakes established, and frontier troops increased.

sentences.zh: 又言：「許浦宜開河三十六里，梅里鎮宜築二大堰，作斗門，遇行師，則決防送船。

translations.literal: He also said: "At Xupu a canal thirty-six li should be opened; at Meili Town two great barrages should be built with sluice gates—when troops march, break the dikes to send boats through.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "At Xupu a canal thirty-six li long should be opened, and at Meili Town two great barrages with sluice gates should be built so that, when troops move, the dikes can be breached to float boats through.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「馮湛創多槳船，底平檣浮，雖尺水可運。

translations.literal: He also said: "Feng Zhan created multi-oar boats, flat-bottomed with floating masts—even a foot of water they can operate.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "Feng Zhan devised multi-oar boats with flat bottoms and floating masts that can operate in as little as a foot of water.

sentences.zh: 今十五六年，修葺數少，不足用。

translations.literal: Now after fifteen or sixteen years, repairs and replacements are few—insufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: Now, fifteen or sixteen years later, too few have been repaired or replaced, and they are no longer adequate.

sentences.zh: 」謂宜募瀕海富商入船予爵，招善操舟者以補水軍，上嘉之。

translations.literal: He said wealthy merchants on the coast should be recruited to contribute boats in exchange for titles, and skilled boatmen should be enlisted to supplement the navy—the emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed recruiting wealthy coastal merchants to contribute boats in exchange for titles and enlisting skilled boatmen to replenish the navy. The emperor praised the plan.

sentences.zh: 以提舉佑神觀兼侍講、同修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Superintendent of the Youshen Shrine concurrently Lecturer and co-compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed superintendent of the Youshen Shrine, concurrently lecturer and co-compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 邁初入史館，預修《四朝帝紀》，進敷文閣直學士、直學士院。

translations.literal: When Mai first entered the History Institute, he participated in compiling the Records of Four Reigns; he was promoted to Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and of the Hanlin Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Mai first entered the History Institute, he helped compile the Records of Four Reigns and was promoted to academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and the Hanlin Institute.

sentences.zh: 講讀官宿直，上時召入，談論至夜分。

translations.literal: As lecturing official on overnight duty, the emperor would summon him in from time to time, discussing until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: On nights when he was on duty as lecturing official, the emperor would summon him and talk until midnight.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，拜翰林學士，遂上《四朝史》，一祖八宗百七十八年為一書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was appointed Hanlin Academician and submitted the History of Four Reigns—one ancestor, eight emperors, 178 years as one work.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was appointed Hanlin academician and submitted the History of Four Reigns, covering one founding ancestor, eight emperors, and 178 years in a single work.

sentences.zh: 紹熙改元，進煥章閣學士、知紹興府。

translations.literal: When the Shaoxi reign era was inaugurated, he was promoted to Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and appointed to govern Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shaoxi reign era was inaugurated in 1190, he was promoted to academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and appointed prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 過闕奏事，言新政宜以十漸為戒。

translations.literal: Passing the capital to report on affairs, he said the new policies should take ten gradual warnings as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital to report on affairs, he warned that the new policies should heed his Ten Gradual Deteriorations.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「浙東民困於和市，卿往，為朕正之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The people of eastern Zhejiang suffer from the market purchase system—you go, and rectify it for Us.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The people of eastern Zhejiang are suffering under the forced-purchase system. Go and set that right for me.

sentences.zh: 」邁再拜曰：「誓盡力。

translations.literal: Mai bowed twice and said: "I vow to exert my utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai bowed twice and said: "I swear to do my utmost.

sentences.zh: 」邁至郡，核實詭戶四萬八千三百有奇，所減絹以匹計者，略如其數。

translations.literal: Arriving at the prefecture, he verified fraudulent household registrations—48,300-odd; the silk reduced, counted in bolts, roughly matched that number.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the prefecture, he verified more than 48,300 fraudulent household registrations, and the silk tax reduction, counted in bolts, roughly matched that figure.

sentences.zh: 提舉玉隆萬壽宮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Superintendent of the Yulong Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed superintendent of the Yulong Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年，再上章告老，進龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: The next year he again submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was promoted to Academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again memorialized to retire and was promoted to academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 尋以端明殿學士致仕，是歲卒，年八十。

translations.literal: Soon after he retired as Academician of the Duanming Hall; that year he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he retired as academician of the Duanming Hall. That same year he died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫，諡文敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness and given the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 邁兄弟皆以文章取盛名，躋貴顯，邁尤以博洽受知孝宗，謂其文備眾體。

translations.literal: The Mai brothers all gained great fame through literary works and rose to eminent rank; Mai especially, through encyclopedic learning, won Emperor Xiaozong's favor—the emperor said his writings encompassed every genre.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong brothers all won great fame through their writing and rose to high office. Hong Mai especially, through encyclopedic learning, won Emperor Xiaozong's favor; the emperor said his writings mastered every genre.

sentences.zh: 邁考閱典故，漁獵經史，極鬼神事物之變，手書《資治通鑑》凡三。

translations.literal: Mai examined and reviewed institutional precedents, ranged widely through classics and histories, exhaustively treating transformations of spirits, ghosts, and things; he hand-copied the Comprehensive Mirror three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai reviewed institutional precedents and ranged widely through the classics and histories, exploring transformations of spirits, ghosts, and natural phenomena to their limits. He hand-copied the Comprehensive Mirror in full three times.

sentences.zh: 有《容齋五筆》、《夷堅志》行於世，其他著述尤多。

translations.literal: He had Rongzhai's Five Notes and Yijian Records circulating in the world; his other writings were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His Rongzhai's Five Notes and Records of Yijian circulated widely, and his other writings were even more numerous.

sentences.zh: 所修《欽宗紀》多本之孫覿，附耿南仲，惡李綱，所紀多失實，故朱熹舉王允之論，言佞臣不可使執筆，以為不當取覿所紀云。

translations.literal: The Record of Emperor Qinzong that he compiled relied heavily on Sun Di, who sided with Geng Nanzhong and opposed Li Gang—what was recorded was often untrue; therefore Zhu Xi cited Wang Yun's argument that flatterers must not be allowed to wield the brush, holding that Sun Di's account should not have been taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Emperor Qinzong that he compiled relied heavily on Sun Di, who sided with Geng Nanzhong and opposed Li Gang, so much of it was inaccurate. Zhu Xi therefore cited Wang Yun's argument that sycophants must not be allowed to wield the brush, holding that Sun Di's account should not have been used.

sentences.zh: 論曰：孔子云：「使於四方，不辱君命，可謂士矣。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Confucius said: "Sent to the four directions, not disgracing the lord's commission—such a one may be called a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Confucius said, "One sent on missions to the four directions who does not disgrace his ruler's commission may be called a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 」當建炎、紹興之際，凡使金者，如探虎口，能全節而歸，若朱弁、張邵、洪皓其庶幾乎，望之不足議也。

translations.literal: In the era of Jianyan and Shaoxing, all who served as envoys to the Jin were like probing a tiger's mouth; those who could preserve their integrity and return—Zhu Bian, Zhang Shao, and Hong Hao come close to it; Wangzhi is not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyan and Shaoxing era, serving as envoy to the Jin was like reaching into a tiger's maw. Those who preserved their integrity and returned—Zhu Bian, Zhang Shao, and Hong Hao came closest to that ideal. Zheng Wangzhi is not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 皓留北十五年，忠節尤著，高宗謂蘇武不能過，誠哉。

translations.literal: Hao remained in the north fifteen years; loyalty and integrity were especially remarkable—Emperor Gaozong said Su Wu could not surpass him—truly so.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hao remained in the north for fifteen years, and his loyalty and integrity were especially remarkable. Emperor Gaozong said that even Su Wu could not surpass him—and that was true.

sentences.zh: 然竟以忤秦檜謫死，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yet in the end, for opposing Qin Hui he was banished and died—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he died in exile for having opposed Qin Hui. How tragic!

sentences.zh: 其子适、遵、邁相繼登詞科，文名滿天下，适位極臺輔，而邁文學尤高，立朝議論最多，所謂忠議之報，詎不信夫。

translations.literal: His sons Shi, Zun, and Mai successively passed the literary examination; literary fame filled the world—Shi rose to the highest ministerial rank, while Mai's scholarship was especially lofty and his court deliberations the most numerous—the so-called reward of loyal remonstrance—is it not believable indeed?
translations.idiomatic: His sons Hong Shi, Hong Zun, and Hong Mai passed the literary examination in succession, and their literary fame filled the empire. Hong Shi rose to the highest ministerial rank, while Hong Mai's scholarship was especially distinguished and his court deliberations the most numerous. The reward of loyal remonstrance—can one doubt that it is real?
